title: Hall and Yard
text:
1. The Harborwick 3PL site in Port Sellow consists of a single-storey warehouse hall with a small office annex and an enclosed fenced yard. All warehousing, storage and handling operations take place within this defined perimeter. The dimensions stated in this section are the fixed limits within which both shifts operate.

2. The warehouse hall provides 6,000 m2 of usable floorspace on one level. This area contains all operational zones, internal aisles, racking and staging areas. No storage or handling activity is permitted outside the hall except in the designated yard and dock areas.

3. The hall has a clear internal height of 10 m measured from finished floor level to the underside of the lowest structural or service obstruction. This clear height determines the usable height for high-bay racking in bulk storage and for free block-stacking where permitted. No goods, fixtures or equipment may reduce this clearance in main transport aisles.

4. Adjoining the hall is a small office annex for administration, supervision and system control. The annex is separate from the warehouse floor and does not form part of the 6,000 m2 operational floorspace. Access between office and warehouse is via designated personnel doors only.

5. The fenced yard surrounding the hall covers approximately 3,500 m2. It provides vehicle circulation, queuing and manoeuvring space for inbound and outbound carriers serving the dock doors. The yard is fully fenced with controlled gate access and includes a marked driver waiting area.

6. The building is served by 8 dock doors at a uniform dock height of 1.2 m, each equipped with its own dock leveller. The doors are divided by function: Doors 1-4 are inbound only and Doors 5-8 are outbound only. This separation is fixed and applies to all shifts, including peak-season overtime.

7. Inbound doors 1-4 serve the receiving zone and outbound doors 5-8 serve the dispatch zone. No inbound unloading may take place at an outbound door and no outbound loading may take place at an inbound door. Carrier assignment to a specific door is made only by the dispatcher as part of the scheduled time-slot.

8. The yard layout provides for one-way flow to and from the dock ramps, with pedestrian walkways physically separated from vehicle routes. Drivers reporting for their assigned slot must wait in the marked waiting area in the yard and must not enter the hall. Unauthorised parking or waiting on dock ramps or in transport aisles is not permitted.

9. All dimensions, door allocations and yard boundaries described in this section are to be treated as site capacity limits. Shift supervisors must plan receiving, storage, picking and dispatch activity so that hall floorspace, dock availability and yard circulation are not exceeded at any time during the shift.

title: Floor Zones A–F
text:
1. The warehouse floor is divided into six fixed zones, designated Zone A through Zone F. This zone map is taught on day one and is used for all movement, storage and documentation. Every location, task and record must refer to its zone by number.

2. Zone A — receiving — covers 800 m2 at the inbound side of the hall and serves Doors 1-4. All inbound vehicles unload, count and inspection activity takes place in Zone A. No goods may move past Zone A to any other zone until paperwork has been checked and inspection is complete.

3. Zone B — bulk storage — covers 2,200 m2 and contains the high-bay pallet racking. Zone B provides 2,400 pallet positions for bulk stock. Each rack bay in Zone B is rated to a maximum of 2,700 kg. Where goods in Zone B are held in free block-stacking outside racking, stacking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m overall height.

4. Zone C — picking — covers 1,200 m2 and contains ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Zone C is the only zone where customer order picking is carried out. Pick faces in Zone C are replenished from bulk stock held in Zone B before each picking shift.

5. Zone D — dispatch — covers 900 m2 at the outbound side of the hall in front of Doors 5-8. Zone D is used solely for outbound staging. Only wrapped and labelled pallets that have been released for loading may be staged in Zone D prior to loading.

6. Zone E — cold zone — covers 300 m2 and provides chilled storage. Zone E is held between +2 °C and +8 °C at all times, with continuous temperature alarms and a manual temperature verification carried out each shift. Only goods requiring chilled storage may be held in Zone E.

7. Zone F — services and control — covers 600 m2 and houses value-added packing, quarantine and returns inspection. All returns inspection and quarantine activity takes place in Zone F. No quarantine or returns stock may be held outside Zone F.

8. Within Zone F is a separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2. All hazardous materials on site must be stored inside this cage in Zone F and never in any other zone. The total quantity of hazmat in the cage in Zone F must never exceed 4,000 kg at any time.

9. The six zones together account for the full 6,000 m2 of hall floorspace: Zone A 800 m2, Zone B 2,200 m2, Zone C 1,200 m2, Zone D 900 m2, Zone E 300 m2 and Zone F 600 m2. Zone boundaries are permanently marked on the floor and on overhead signage, and staff must not store, stage or operate outside the zone designated for that activity.

title: Docks and Yard Access
text:
### ops.ch01.s3 Docks and Yard Access

1. The eight dock doors provide the only interface between road vehicles and the warehouse hall. All loading and unloading takes place at the doors; no direct vehicle entry into the hall and no handling of goods in the yard is permitted at any time.

2. No carrier may approach a door without a pre-booked time slot and a specific door assignment from the dispatcher. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling and sequences all arrivals to match receiving capacity in Zone A and staging capacity in Zone D. Carriers arriving early or without a slot must wait at the gate until instructed to proceed.

3. Doors 1-4 are inbound only and open directly into Zone A. Only inbound unloading, count and inspection activity may take place at these doors. No outbound loading, staging or empty-pallet collection may be scheduled or carried out at Doors 1-4, even during peak overtime.

4. Doors 5-8 are outbound only and open directly into Zone D. Only outbound staging and loading of wrapped and labelled pallets released by the dispatcher may take place at these doors. No inbound receipts, returns or quarantine movements may be scheduled at Doors 5-8.

5. Drivers must report to the marked waiting area in the fenced yard on arrival and remain there until called forward to their assigned door. Drivers are not permitted to enter the hall, walk in transport aisles, or wait on dock ramps or levellers. Access to the warehouse floor is restricted to authorised Harborwick staff wearing required PPE.

6. The fenced yard of approximately 3,500 m2 is under controlled gate access and operates as a one-way circulation system around the dock ramps. Inbound traffic approaches Doors 1-4 from the designated inbound lane and outbound traffic departs from Doors 5-8 via the outbound lane. Parking or queuing on ramps, crossings or in front of pedestrian barriers is prohibited, and any vehicle not at its assigned door must use the marked waiting area.

7. Each dock door is equipped with its own dock leveller at the uniform dock height of 1.2 m. Levellers are operated only by trained staff and only when a vehicle is correctly positioned and braked at the door. Faults, damage or uneven seating of a leveller must be reported to the shift supervisor and maintenance technician immediately, and the door taken out of service until cleared.

8. Pedestrian and vehicle movements are physically separated at the docks. Yellow-barrier walkways 1.2 m wide provide the only pedestrian routes to and from the door areas, with marked crossings at each ramp. Transport aisles feeding the doors are 4.0 m wide and must be kept clear for forklift and pallet-jack movement. Drivers on foot moving between cab and trailer must use the walkways and crossings and must not cross behind reversing vehicles.

9. Yard traffic is limited to 12 km/h, with 5 km/h enforced at all marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Building speed of 10 km/h applies as soon as a truck-mounted load or MHE enters the hall. The shift supervisor is responsible for enforcing door discipline, waiting-area compliance and yard speed limits on every shift.

title: Roles on Site
text:
### ops.ch02.s1 Roles on Site

1. Harborwick 3PL operates with around 38-40 staff on two daily shifts within a fixed role structure. Every activity on the floor is tied to a named role and its zone. No staff member may perform a task outside their role unless formally reassigned by the shift supervisor for that shift.

2. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site — operations, safety and final sign-offs. The manager owns the overall plan for receiving, storage, picking and dispatch across all zones, ensures procedures PR-01 to PR-15 are followed, and retains sole authority to authorise new forklift operators and to approve overtime.

3. Two shift supervisors provide continuous floor leadership, one per shift from 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, with cover for Saturday overtime in peak season. The shift supervisor on duty is in charge of the floor: directing staff in Zones A to F, enforcing zone discipline, managing dock and yard compliance, and leading immediate incident response.

4. Eight forklift operators carry out all mechanised handling. They operate the 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t and 11 electric pallet jacks for put-away to Zone B, replenishment to Zone C, and movement of wrapped pallets to Zone D. No other role may drive counterbalance or reach trucks.

5. Six inbound operators work exclusively in Zone A at Doors 1-4. They unload inbound vehicles, count and inspect goods against paperwork, and prepare inspected goods for system booking. No goods may leave Zone A until inbound operators have completed count and inspection.

6. Ten pickers work in Zone C against WMS scanner tasks. They pick from ground-level pick faces and flow racks, scan-verify every item, and move picked goods for packing, labelling and transfer to Zone D. Pickers do not replenish their own faces and do not handle put-away to bulk storage.

7. Two stock controllers own inventory accuracy day to day. They execute the rotating daily cycle counts, conduct second counts and recounts, and prepare adjustments for approval. They control stock accuracy in Zone B, Zone E and Zone F locations and ensure the system reflects the stock on the rack.

8. Four returns and packing staff operate in Zone F. They receive and inspect all returns and quarantined goods, assess each unit, and propose disposition as restock, rework or scrap. They also carry out value-added packing tasks in Zone F before goods are returned to stock or removed.

9. One maintenance technician is responsible for the upkeep of all MHE, racking and dock equipment including levellers, stretch wrappers and the cardboard baler. The technician carries out planned checks, responds to faults reported from the floor, and logs every repair with date, equipment and action taken.

10. Two dispatchers control transport and outbound flow. They book carriers, assign every inbound and outbound vehicle a specific door and time slot, sequence arrivals to match Zone A and Zone D capacity, and release outbound loads for loading at Doors 5-8. No vehicle may be loaded or unloaded without dispatcher release.

11. Two floaters provide absence and peak cover across inbound, picking and packing tasks as directed by the shift supervisor. Floaters work only within roles for which they are trained and authorised, and never operate forklifts or reach trucks unless licensed and specifically authorised as forklift operators.

title: Approvals and Accountability
text:
### ops.ch02.s2 Approvals and Accountability

1. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site — operations, safety and compliance with procedures PR-01 to PR-15 across Zones A to F. This accountability is not delegable. Shift supervisors, dispatchers and all other roles act within authorities expressly granted in this section, and any matter outside those authorities must be escalated to the manager.

2. Only the warehouse manager may authorise a new forklift operator. Authorisation requires a valid licence and documented practical assessment, and is recorded with date and equipment types before the operator may drive any of the 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t or powered pallet trucks. No other role may grant or extend driving authority.

3. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime. This includes any extension beyond the two-shift pattern of 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and any Saturday morning working in peak season. Requests from shift supervisors or dispatchers have no effect until signed by the manager.

4. The warehouse manager signs off the results of the annual wall-to-wall stocktake. No stocktake is closed and no system-wide adjustment arising from it is posted until the manager has reviewed the count sheets, recounts and variance report and applied a dated signature.

5. Damaged-goods write-offs are approved by value threshold. The shift supervisor on duty may approve a write-off up to and including 750 EUR per incident. Any write-off above 750 EUR, individually or aggregated for the same incident, requires the warehouse manager's written approval. Goods remain in quarantine in Zone F until the applicable approval is recorded.

6. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns in Zone F. Returns and packing staff inspect every unit and propose restock, rework or scrap, but no unit is returned to Zone B, Zone C or Zone E, sent for rework, or scrapped until the shift supervisor has approved the proposal and logged the decision.

7. Every incident on the floor — injury, near-miss, MHE contact, rack damage, spill or temperature alarm — is reviewed by the shift supervisor on duty. The supervisor ensures the incident report is completed, immediate containment is in place, and escalation to the warehouse manager and maintenance technician is made where required. No report is filed as closed without the supervisor's review signature.

8. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling. Only the dispatcher may assign a carrier a specific door and time slot and release a load for inbound unloading at Doors 1-4 or outbound loading at Doors 5-8. Floor staff must not direct a vehicle to a different door or change the sequence without dispatcher re-authorisation.

9. All approvals under this section must be documented with name, role, date and signature in the relevant system record or paper log. Verbal approvals are not valid. Where a threshold is stated, the threshold value is inclusive of the lower approver's limit, and any attempt to split a single event to avoid the higher approval is prohibited.

title: Shift Leadership and Dock Control
text:
### ops.ch02.s3 Shift Leadership and Dock Control

1. One shift supervisor is in charge of the floor at all times the hall is operating. The morning shift runs 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, with Saturday morning overtime added in peak season only. There is never a period of operation without a named supervisor in charge.

2. The shift supervisor on duty directs all floor staff in Zones A to F for that shift: inbound operators in Zone A, forklift operators moving between Zones A, B, C and D, pickers in Zone C, and returns and packing staff in Zone F. The supervisor assigns tasks within trained roles, enforces zone discipline, and ensures handover between shifts is complete.

3. The supervisor is responsible for immediate incident response on the floor. This includes stopping work where needed, securing racking, MHE or dock equipment, initiating evacuation and roll call when required, and ensuring every incident report is completed and reviewed before close. Escalation to the warehouse manager and maintenance technician is made where thresholds are met.

4. The supervisor enforces site rules on the floor, including mandatory high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear for everyone on the warehouse floor, seat-belt use by forklift operators when moving, and speed compliance of 10 km/h inside the building, 12 km/h in the yard, and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Non-compliance is stopped and logged.

5. Dock control is owned solely by the dispatcher role. The dispatcher books all inbound and outbound carriers, issues each a pre-booked time slot and a specific door assignment, and sequences arrivals to match capacity in Zone A for receiving and Zone D for dispatch. No other role may set or change the dock schedule.

6. Doors 1-4 are inbound only and open into Zone A; Doors 5-8 are outbound only and open from Zone D. The dispatcher assigns inbound carriers to Doors 1-4 and outbound carriers to Doors 5-8 at 1.2 m dock height, each with its own leveller. Floor staff must not redirect a vehicle to a different door or alter the sequence without dispatcher re-authorisation.

7. No vehicle may be unloaded at Doors 1-4 or loaded at Doors 5-8 without dispatcher release. For inbound, release follows document check readiness in Zone A; for outbound, release follows confirmation that pallets are wrapped, labelled and staged in Zone D. Levellers are operated only by trained staff when the vehicle is correctly positioned and braked.

8. Drivers must report on arrival to the marked waiting area in the fenced yard and remain there until called forward to their assigned door. Drivers are not permitted to enter the hall, walk in transport aisles, or wait on dock ramps. The supervisor enforces waiting-area discipline and yard circulation, while the dispatcher controls gate call-forward timing.

9. The supervisor and dispatcher work as complementary controls: the dispatcher owns the plan for who arrives at which door and when, and the supervisor owns compliance and safety of execution on the floor and in the yard. Any conflict over capacity, delay or vehicle readiness is resolved between them on shift and escalated to the warehouse manager if the schedule or overtime approval is affected.

title: Working Hours
text:
### ops.ch03.s1 Working Hours

1. Harborwick 3PL operates on a fixed two-shift pattern covering the warehouse hall Monday to Friday. The morning shift runs 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift runs 14:00-22:00. These times define the normal operating window of the site: no receiving, picking, packing or dispatch activity takes place outside these hours without approved overtime.

2. The site is closed for normal operations on Saturdays and Sundays. The only exception is authorised Saturday morning overtime in peak season. Saturday overtime is not rostered by default and does not create a third shift; it is an extension of peak capacity within the existing zone and door structure.

3. Each shift is led by one named shift supervisor who is in charge of the floor. The morning supervisor assumes charge at 06:00 and hands over to the afternoon supervisor at 14:00. The afternoon supervisor retains charge until 22:00 close. There is no period of live operation in the hall without a supervisor in charge, including during any approved overtime.

4. All floor roles work within this shift pattern: forklift operators, inbound operators in Zone A, pickers in Zone C, stock controllers, returns and packing staff in Zone F, dispatchers and floaters. The office annex follows the same Monday to Friday daytime pattern for administration and system control, with dispatcher cover aligned to dock activity.

5. Shift start and finish times are fixed and apply to all zones and docks. Work at Doors 1-4 inbound and Doors 5-8 outbound, movement in Zones A to F, and yard circulation must be planned to start and stop within the published shift times. Vehicles are not called forward to a door outside the operating window unless overtime has been approved.

6. Only the warehouse manager may authorise extra time. This includes any extension beyond 06:00-14:00 or 14:00-22:00 on weekdays and any Saturday morning working in peak season. A request from a shift supervisor, dispatcher or any other role has no effect until the manager has recorded written approval with name, date and signature.

7. Overtime is approved per occasion, per shift and per team required. Approval specifies the date, the hours, the zones to be worked and the reason. Staff must not start early, finish late or attend on Saturday on the assumption that approval will follow. The shift supervisor must verify that approval is in place before tasking staff for overtime.

8. The manager's control of overtime is absolute for resourcing and compliance. No other role may grant overtime, extend a shift informally, or split overtime across days to avoid approval. Unauthorised extra time is treated as a procedural breach and is logged by the shift supervisor for review.

9. In peak season, Saturday morning overtime is used only to clear inbound backlog in Zone A, replenish Zone C, or release staged outbound loads from Zone D where weekday capacity of 4 outbound doors at 4 trailer loads per shift has been fully utilised. The dispatcher adjusts door slots and the supervisor adjusts zone tasking within the approved Saturday hours, with the same zone discipline, speed limits and PPE rules as on weekdays.

title: End-of-Shift Handover
text:
### ops.ch03.s2 End-of-Shift Handover

1. Every change of shift is controlled by PR-15 End-of-Shift Handover, which is a face-to-face handover between the outgoing and incoming shift supervisor. The morning supervisor hands over to the afternoon supervisor at 14:00 and the afternoon supervisor secures the site at 22:00 and records the night handover for the next morning supervisor at 06:00. There is no unsupervised gap at shift change.

2. The handover takes place on the warehouse floor and is recorded in the shift handover log with names, roles, date, time and both signatures. Verbal handovers, telephone hand-ins or unsigned log entries are not valid. No incoming supervisor may assume charge until the log for the previous shift has been reviewed and signed.

3. The outgoing supervisor reports the operational state of every zone: inbound queue and documents checked in Zone A, pallets held or blocked for put-away in Zone B including any bay exceeding caution load, replenishment status of pick faces in Zone C, wrapped and labelled pallets staged and loads released or still pending in Zone D, chilled stock and last temperature verification in Zone E, and quarantine, returns and hazmat quantity in Zone F. Any deviation from zone discipline is logged.

4. The dispatcher schedule is handed over as part of PR-15. This includes carriers already assigned a door and time slot at Doors 1-4 inbound and Doors 5-8 outbound, arrivals delayed or waiting in the marked waiting area, doors out of service due to leveller or equipment fault, and any conflict between Zone A capacity and Zone D staging that requires re-sequencing. No vehicle may be called forward without dispatcher release confirmed in the handover.

5. All safety and equipment matters are included: MHE availability and any truck grounded after the daily documented check, racking damage or monthly inspection flags, spill or hazmat cage status against the 4,000 kg limit, temperature alarms in Zone E, and any incident, near-miss or injury with its incident report status. If an incident report is open for review, that is stated and the action owner is named.

6. Inventory accuracy is handed over explicitly: cycle counts completed that shift on the rotating zone schedule, any second count or recount pending, adjustments awaiting approval, and the location of quarantined and damaged goods in Zone F. Goods that arrived that shift and have not yet been booked into the system remain identified in Zone A and must not be presented as available stock.

7. The outgoing supervisor confirms housekeeping, PPE compliance and pedestrian controls: high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear compliance, forklift seat-belt use, speed compliance at 10 km/h in the hall, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, and that 1.2 m walkways and 4.0 m transport aisles are clear. Any stop-work, clean-up or barrier repair required is handed over as an open task.

8. The incoming supervisor acknowledges receipt by signature and thereafter owns the floor and incident response until the next handover. Any task logged as incomplete becomes the incoming supervisor's responsibility to task, monitor and close. Matters beyond the supervisor's authority, including overtime need, write-offs above 750 EUR and annual stocktake sign-off, are flagged for escalation to the warehouse manager.

9. At 22:00 close the afternoon supervisor completes the end-of-day PR-15 entry, secures dock doors and levellers, verifies that Zone E temperature is within +2 °C to +8 °C and alarmed, confirms the hazmat cage is locked and within limit, and leaves the hall and yard in a safe state for restart at 06:00. The site may not be reopened or operated outside 06:00-22:00 without prior written overtime approval from the warehouse manager recorded in the log.

title: Arrival and Door Assignment
text:
### ops.ch04.s1 Arrival and Door Assignment

1. Arrival and door assignment is governed by PR-01 Inbound Receiving and is owned by the dispatcher. No inbound carrier may enter the fenced yard circulation or approach Doors 1-4 without a pre-booked time slot and a specific door assignment issued by the dispatcher. Early or unbooked arrivals must wait at the gate until instructed.

2. The dispatcher sequences all inbound arrivals to match receiving capacity in Zone A. Each inbound vehicle is assigned one door from Doors 1-4, each at 1.2 m dock height with its own leveller, and one time slot. Assignments are communicated to the shift supervisor and recorded in the dock schedule before the shift starts.

3. On arrival at the gate, the driver reports carrier, client and purchase-order or ASN reference to the dispatcher. The dispatcher confirms the booked door and slot, checks that Zone A can receive, and directs the vehicle to the marked waiting area in the 3,500 m2 yard. The driver must remain in the waiting area and must not enter the hall.

4. Vehicles are called forward from the waiting area to their assigned inbound door only on dispatcher instruction. The call-forward follows strict yard one-way flow to Doors 1-4 via the inbound lane. No vehicle may self-select a door, swap doors, or queue on dock ramps or pedestrian crossings.

5. The vehicle must be correctly positioned, braked and chocked at the assigned door before the leveller is deployed. Levellers are operated only by trained Harborwick staff after the shift supervisor confirms position. Any leveller fault, uneven seating or vehicle movement is reported immediately and the door is taken out of service until cleared by maintenance.

6. PR-01 requires that documents are checked before anything is unloaded. The inbound operator assigned to that door attends Zone A at Doors 1-4, checks the delivery note, purchase order and carrier paperwork against the dispatcher schedule while the vehicle remains sealed, and verifies client, product, quantity expected and any temperature or hazmat note.

7. No unloading may start until the document check is complete and recorded. If paperwork is missing, mismatched or requires manager escalation, the load remains on the vehicle in the door and the dispatcher and shift supervisor are notified. Goods must not be unloaded, counted or moved past Zone A pending resolution.

8. Once paperwork is confirmed, the dispatcher releases the door for unloading and the shift supervisor authorises the inbound team to break the seal and start unload, count and inspection in Zone A. The release, door number, carrier and time are logged with name and signature as the PR-01 start point for that receipt.

9. Drivers on foot between cab and trailer must use the 1.2 m yellow-barrier walkways and marked crossings and must not walk in 4.0 m transport aisles or behind reversing vehicles. Yard speed of 12 km/h and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps is enforced by the shift supervisor throughout arrival and door assignment.

title: Unloading, Count and Inspection
text:
### ops.ch04.s2 Unloading, Count and Inspection

1. Unloading, count and inspection in Zone A is the controlled continuation of PR-01 Inbound Receiving. Following document check and dispatcher release for Doors 1-4, only the assigned inbound operators may break the seal and commence unloading. No goods may be moved past Zone A until count and inspection are complete and recorded.

2. Unloading is carried out by inbound operators using electric pallet jacks or hand pallet jacks and, where required, a counterbalance forklift rated at 3.0 t operated only by an authorised forklift operator. All activity remains in the 800 m2 receiving area in front of Doors 1-4. Levellers at 1.2 m dock height are operated only by trained staff after the vehicle is positioned, braked and confirmed by the shift supervisor.

3. Goods are placed directly into the designated Zone A inspection lanes segregated by door number, carrier and purchase order. Pallets remain at floor level and must not be block-stacked above 3 pallets high and 4.0 m where temporarily staged, and no pallet staged may exceed the site limit of 900 kg. Transport aisles of 4.0 m and yellow-barrier walkways of 1.2 m must be kept clear at all times.

4. The inbound operator counts every handling unit against the checked delivery note and dispatcher schedule: number of pallets, cartons per pallet, product code, batch or lot, and quantity per SKU. Any overage, shortage or substitution is noted at the pallet and recorded on the PR-01 receipt record with name, time and signature before further inspection.

5. Every unit is visually inspected in Zone A before any booking. Inspection covers carton integrity, seal and tamper evidence, wet or crushed packaging, labelling match to paperwork, and expiry or date-code where applicable. For goods marked for Zone E, the inbound operator takes a surface temperature reading on arrival; product outside +2 °C to +8 °C is segregated and the shift supervisor and dispatcher notified immediately.

6. Goods that pass count and inspection are marked as inspected and segregated in Zone A as ready for system booking. Goods that fail on quantity variance, damage, temperature excursion, incorrect product or suspected contamination are segregated within Zone A as held, labelled HOLD and are not presented as available stock. Hazmat arriving without correct documentation or outside the 4,000 kg cage limit in Zone F is not unloaded beyond the door and is escalated to the shift supervisor.

7. All discrepancies, damages and holds are reported on shift to the shift supervisor and dispatcher and entered in the PR-01 log. Chilled goods requiring Zone E and hazardous goods requiring the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F retain their hold in Zone A until the supervisor confirms the receiving location can accept them. No held pallet may be released to put-away to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F until the disposition is recorded.

8. Damaged goods identified during inspection are transferred to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, in accordance with PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. They remain in quarantine pending write-off approval by value threshold and are not booked as available. Returns staff in Zone F do not assess inbound receipts; their role is limited to returns handling.

9. Only inspected goods that have passed count and inspection in Zone A may proceed to system booking under PR-01. The inbound operator signs the count and inspection record as the control point, and the shift supervisor verifies that held and damaged goods are segregated and that no uninspected goods have left Zone A. Uninspected or uncounted goods must never be booked into the system.

title: System Booking and Release to Put-Away
text:
### ops.ch04.s3 System Booking and Release to Put-Away

1. System booking and release to put-away is the formal gate between Zone A and Zones B, E and F under PR-01 Inbound Receiving. No pallet may leave the 800 m2 receiving area for put-away until it has passed count and inspection in Zone A and has been booked into the WMS. Only booked goods may be moved to bulk storage, cold zone or services and control.

2. Booking is carried out in Zone A immediately after inspection by the assigned inbound operator using one of the 20 handheld WMS scanners. The operator books from the signed PR-01 count and inspection record; the quantity booked must match the quantity counted and inspected, by pallet, carton and SKU, with batch or lot and expiry where applicable. No estimated, expected or paperwork quantity may be booked.

3. Only goods marked as inspected and passed in Zone A may be booked as available stock. Goods segregated as held for quantity variance, temperature excursion, incorrect product or documentation query, and goods identified as damaged, are not booked as available. Held pallets remain labelled HOLD in Zone A pending disposition; damaged pallets are not booked and are transferred to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

4. On booking, the WMS creates the system receipt, allocates the put-away location and generates the pallet licence label. Allocation follows product type: ambient bulk to Zone B racking or block-stack, chilled goods to Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C, and hazardous, quarantine or returns-related goods to Zone F. The label records client, SKU, quantity, batch, receipt reference and target zone and must be applied and scan-verified before movement.

5. The shift supervisor verifies the booking before release. Verification confirms that the PR-01 document check, count and inspection entries are signed, that held and damaged pallets are segregated, that the WMS receipt matches the inspected quantity, and that the allocated location can accept the load within site limits of 900 kg per pallet, 2,700 kg per rack bay in Zone B, 3 pallets high and 4.0 m for block-stacking, and 4,000 kg total in the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F.

6. Release to put-away is the handover from PR-01 to PR-02 Put-away to Storage. The shift supervisor records release in the PR-01 log with door number, pallet IDs, target zones and signature. Only after this release may forklift operators using the 3.0 t counterbalance forklifts or 2.0 t reach trucks, or other authorised MHE, move the labelled pallets from Zone A. No goods may be released on verbal instruction.

7. No release may exceed location capacity or cage limits. Pallets over 900 kg, loads that would take a rack bay over 2,700 kg, chilled goods without a confirmed Zone E location held at +2 °C to +8 °C with alarms active, or hazmat that would take the cage in Zone F over 4,000 kg must be held in Zone A and escalated to the shift supervisor and dispatcher for re-allocation. Hazmat may only be allocated to the cage and never to Zones B, C, D or E.

8. Movement from Zone A to Zone B, E or F is by the designated 4.0 m transport aisles with scan confirmation at both ends. The forklift operator scans the pallet licence on departure from Zone A and on arrival at the allocated location in Zone B, E or F. The WMS updates stock on the rack only after the arrival scan; physical put-away in the location completes the booking.

9. The PR-01 record, WMS receipt, pallet labels and scan history together form the audit trail for the gate. They show who counted, inspected, booked, verified and moved each pallet and when. Any pallet remaining in Zone A without a booking at shift handover is reported in the PR-15 handover as unbooked and is not presented as available stock until the booking and release steps are complete.

title: Bulk Storage in Zone B
text:
### ops.ch05.s1 Bulk Storage in Zone B

1. Zone B bulk storage is governed by PR-02 Put-away to Storage and covers 2,200 m2 of the hall. It contains the high-bay pallet racking with 2,400 pallet positions and designated block-stack areas for overflow. No other zone may be used for bulk storage, and only goods booked in the WMS as available stock may be held in Zone B.

2. Every pallet placed in Zone B must respect the site limit of 900 kg per pallet, load included. Each rack bay in Zone B is rated to a maximum of 2,700 kg total. This means a bay may hold at most three full-weight pallets at 900 kg each; any configuration that would exceed 2,700 kg in a single bay is prohibited and must be re-allocated by the shift supervisor before put-away.

3. Where goods in Zone B are held in free block-stacking outside the racking, stacking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m overall height, including the pallet. Block-stacks must be vertical, stable and within marked floor locations that do not obstruct the 4.0 m main transport aisles or the 3.0 m rack-storage aisles. No block-stack may reduce the 10 m clear height in main transport aisles.

4. Put-away to Zone B is only from Zone A following system booking and shift-supervisor release under PR-01. The WMS allocation specifies the Zone B target location by bay, level and position. The forklift operator must scan the pallet licence on departure from Zone A and scan-verify on arrival at the allocated location; stock is confirmed on the rack only after the arrival scan.

5. Mechanised put-away in Zone B is carried out only by authorised forklift operators. The 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t are used for high-bay placement and retrieval in the racking; the 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t are used for general movement and block-stack placement. No other role may drive counterbalance or reach trucks in Zone B.

6. Forklifts and pallet jacks in Zone B operate within the permanent aisle network: 4.0 m wide main transport aisles feeding Zone B and 3.0 m wide rack-storage aisles between rack rows. Aisles must be kept clear at all times. Goods, empty pallets, wrapping film or idle MHE must not be staged in any aisle, and rack bays must not be overfilled beyond their beam or height envelope.

7. No hazardous materials may be stored in Zone B at any time. All hazmat is stored only in the separate 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F subject to the 4,000 kg cage limit. No chilled goods requiring +2 °C to +8 °C may be held in Zone B; they are allocated to Zone E. Damaged or quarantined goods are not held in Zone B and are transferred to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found.

8. Stock accuracy in Zone B is owned by the stock controllers. Zone B locations are subject to cycle counts every working day on the rotating zone schedule under PR-08, with no adjustment posted without a second count. The shift supervisor verifies put-away completion at handover and reports any stock remaining in Zone A without a booking as unbooked, not available.

9. Zone B racking is subject to documented safety inspection every month by the maintenance technician, with damage, overload or impact logged and the bay taken out of service until cleared. Any bay found at or above its caution load, any rack impact, and any MHE contact is reported to the shift supervisor immediately and handed over under PR-15. Racking pending repair must be physically blocked and not used for put-away.

title: Cold Zone E
text:
### ops.ch05.s2 Cold Zone E

1. Zone E is governed by PR-12 Cold-chain handling and covers 300 m2 of enclosed chilled storage. It is held continuously between +2 °C and +8 °C and is monitored by continuous automatic temperature alarms. Only goods that require chilled storage may be held in Zone E, and no ambient, quarantine or hazmat stock may be stored there at any time.

2. All goods entering Zone E arrive only from Zone A after count, inspection and system booking under PR-01. During inbound inspection in Zone A the inbound operator takes a surface temperature reading of chilled consignments; any product outside +2 °C to +8 °C on arrival is segregated as held in Zone A, labelled HOLD, and escalated to the shift supervisor and dispatcher. No chilled goods outside range are booked as available or released to Zone E.

3. Release to Zone E is by shift supervisor verification only. The supervisor confirms the PR-01 document check and inspection are signed, the WMS receipt matches the inspected quantity, a valid Zone E location is allocated, and the pallet does not exceed the site limit of 900 kg. Only after this release and WMS labelling may the load be moved to Zone E by authorised MHE via the 4.0 m transport aisles with scan on departure from Zone A and scan on arrival in Zone E.

4. Zone E is kept closed except for put-away, replenishment issue and cycle counting. Doors must be kept closed and sealed when not in active use, and must never be blocked open, wedged or obstructed by pallets, MHE or staging. Door open time is to be minimised, and no staging or picking activity for non-chilled goods may take place inside the cold zone.

5. Temperature control in Zone E is by continuous alarmed monitoring backed by a manual verification each shift. The shift supervisor ensures a trained operator records the displayed temperature at least once per shift — morning 06:00-14:00 and afternoon 14:00-22:00 — with zone, reading, date, time, name and signature in the PR-12 log. Any alarm between verifications is treated as an immediate excursion.

6. On any alarm or manual reading outside +2 °C to +8 °C, the shift supervisor stops all put-away and issue for Zone E, secures the doors, notifies the warehouse manager and maintenance technician, and segregates affected stock in place as held. No held chilled stock may be released to picking in Zone C, to dispatch in Zone D or back to bulk storage until the cause is rectified, temperature is restored and documented, and disposition is recorded under PR-12.

7. Storage in Zone E must remain within marked locations and must not obstruct the 4.0 m transport aisle access, the 3.0 m internal aisles where provided, or the alarm sensors and air circulation units. Pallets must not exceed 900 kg and must be stable and within the rack or floor location envelope. Damaged or leaking chilled goods found in Zone E are transferred to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09 and are not retained in Zone E.

8. Stock accuracy in Zone E is owned by the stock controllers under PR-08, with cycle counts carried out on the rotating zone schedule. Counts in Zone E are planned to minimise door open time and are completed quickly with doors closed between counts; no adjustment is posted without a second count. Quantity held in Zone E is included in the annual wall-to-wall stocktake signed off by the warehouse manager.

9. The maintenance technician owns the refrigeration and alarm equipment for Zone E, responds to all alarms and faults, and logs every repair with date, equipment and action taken. Faults, sensor errors, door seal damage or ice build-up are reported to the shift supervisor immediately and the affected locations taken out of service until cleared. The PR-12 alarm and manual verification logs form the cold-chain audit trail and are handed over at each PR-15 shift handover.

title: Quarantine and Hazmat Cage in Zone F
text:
1. Zone F — services and control — covers 600 m2 and is governed by PR-09 Damaged-goods Handling for quarantine and PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for the hazmat cage. Zone F houses value-added packing, quarantine, returns inspection and, within it, a separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2. All quarantine and all hazmat storage on site takes place only in Zone F.

2. The quarantine area in Zone F holds damaged, suspected-contaminated and held goods segregated from available stock. Any damaged goods found during receiving in Zone A, storage in Zone B, picking in Zone C, dispatch in Zone D or inside Zone E are transferred to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09. Quarantined pallets are labelled HOLD with reason, date and finder, are not booked as available stock, and remain physically segregated until disposition is approved.

3. All hazardous materials on site must be stored inside the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2 in Zone F and never in any other zone — not in Zone A, B, C, D or E, and not elsewhere in Zone F outside the cage. The total quantity in the cage must never exceed 4,000 kg at any time. At the site limit of 900 kg per pallet, this is at most 4 full-weight pallets in the cage at any time.

4. Put-away to Zone F is only from Zone A following count, inspection, system booking and shift-supervisor release under PR-01 to PR-02. The WMS allocates the Zone F target — quarantine location or hazmat cage location — and the pallet licence is scan-verified on departure from Zone A and on arrival in Zone F. Hazmat may only be allocated to the ventilated cage of 60 m2 in Zone F subject to the 4,000 kg limit; any allocation that would exceed 4,000 kg in the cage is prohibited and must be held in Zone A for re-allocation.

5. Quarantine stock and hazmat stock are stored strictly segregated within Zone F. No hazmat may be placed in quarantine locations and no quarantine or general stock may be placed in the hazmat cage. Within the cage, incompatible hazmat classes are segregated by the PR-13 compatibility plan with marked bays, and pallets are placed at floor level without block-stacking that would obscure labels, ventilation or spill containment. Pallets in Zone F must not exceed 900 kg and must not obstruct the 4.0 m transport aisles or access to spill equipment.

6. The hazmat cage of 60 m2 in Zone F is kept locked, ventilated and clearly signed, with access limited to authorised staff under the shift supervisor. The supervisor maintains a live cage inventory by weight and pallet count against the 4,000 kg limit, updated on every put-away and issue. No receipt that would take the cage over 4,000 kg may be released to put-away, and no additional hazmat pallet may be moved into the cage until sufficient weight has been issued and booked out.

7. PR-13 spill response controls the cage in Zone F: suitable spill kits, absorbents and PPE are stationed at the cage entrance, ventilation is checked each shift, and any leak, damaged container or vapour is treated as an immediate incident — the area is cordoned, the shift supervisor is notified, and the maintenance technician is called. No damaged or leaking hazmat container is retained in the cage and none is ever transferred to Zone B, C, D or E.

8. No hazmat may be staged, queued or held outside the ventilated cage of 60 m2 in Zone F, even temporarily in Zone A or Zone D, except for the sealed load on the vehicle at the door before inspection. Any hazmat arriving without correct documentation, with damaged packaging, or that would cause the cage to exceed 4,000 kg is not unloaded beyond the door, remains on the vehicle or segregated as held in Zone A, and is escalated to the shift supervisor and dispatcher for return, re-scheduling or alternative disposition under PR-13.

9. All movements to and from quarantine and to and from the hazmat cage of 60 m2 in Zone F are recorded by WMS scans, PR-09 quarantine tags and PR-13 cage logs with pallet ID, weight, location, name, date and time. Cage quantity against the 4,000 kg limit, cage ventilation and spill-kit status, and all quarantine holdings are handed over at each PR-15 shift handover. Goods in quarantine remain unavailable until the shift supervisor — or the warehouse manager for write-offs above 750 EUR — approves restock, rework or scrap.

title: Replenishment of Pick Faces
text:
### ops.ch06.s1 Replenishment of Pick Faces

1. Replenishment of pick faces in Zone C is governed by PR-03 Replenishment of Pick Faces and is the mandatory preparation for every picking shift. Zone C contains only ground-level pick faces and flow racks; it holds no reserve stock. All replenishment stock is drawn from bulk storage in Zone B and, for chilled SKUs, from Zone E, and is moved to Zone C before picking starts.

2. Replenishment is carried out before each picking shift — ahead of the morning shift at 06:00 and ahead of the afternoon shift at 14:00. The shift supervisor on duty owns the PR-03 plan for that shift, sequences the tasks to match the WMS picking workload, and confirms completion before pickers are released to Zone C. No picking task may start in an aisle until its faces have been replenished and verified.

3. Only authorised forklift operators carry out replenishment. The 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t are used for retrieval from high-bay racking in Zone B and the 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t for general movement to Zone C; electric pallet jacks are used only for low-level transfer where instructed. Pickers do not replenish their own faces and must not enter bulk locations in Zone B or Zone E to pull stock.

4. The WMS generates PR-03 replenishment tasks from the outbound order pool, current Zone C levels and allocations. Each task specifies source location in Zone B or Zone E, SKU, batch or lot and expiry where applicable, quantity required, and target pick face or flow-rack lane in Zone C. Tasks are assigned to operators via the 20 handheld WMS scanners; paper or verbal instruction is not permitted.

5. At the source location the operator scans the pallet licence and location to confirm SKU, quantity and batch, observing the site limit of 900 kg per pallet and the Zone B rack-bay limit of 2,700 kg. Any pallet over 900 kg, any bay that would be left overweight, any damaged carton or any stock showing HOLD or quarantine status is not used for replenishment, and the exception is reported to the shift supervisor for re-allocation.

6. Movement from Zone B or Zone E to Zone C is by the 4.0 m main transport aisles and into the 3.0 m rack-storage aisles serving Zone C, with scan on departure and scan on arrival. Speed limits of 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps apply, and 1.2 m yellow-barrier walkways must be kept clear. Flow-rack feed is from the rear replenishment side only; the picking side in Zone C remains clear for pickers.

7. At Zone C the operator places the required quantity into the allocated pick face or flow lane, respecting FIFO by expiry or batch as shown on the task, and ensures labels, location markers and stock are visible and stable. Pallets must not be double-stacked in pick faces, must not obstruct the aisles, and empty pallets and film are removed immediately. Chilled replenishment from Zone E is moved quickly with Zone E doors closed except for access.

8. The operator scan-confirms put to the Zone C location; the WMS updates the face quantity only on this arrival scan. Under-stocks, over-stocks, misplaced stock or damage found in the face are corrected and logged as a PR-03 exception with location, SKU, quantity, reason, name and time. No correction is made by adjustment without a second count by a stock controller under PR-08.

9. The shift supervisor verifies PR-03 completion before releasing picking: all tasks completed or explicitly carried over, exceptions cleared, Zone C faces filled to the planned level, and transport aisles and flow-rack areas clear. Completion with name, time and signature is recorded in the PR-03 log and handed over under PR-15. Any face not replenished is flagged as unavailable in the WMS and is not assigned to pickers until replenished.

title: Order Picking in Zone C
text:
1. Order picking in Zone C is governed by PR-04 Order picking and is carried out only in Zone C. Zone C covers 1,200 m2 and contains ground-level pick faces and flow racks replenished from Zone B and, for chilled SKUs, from Zone E. No picking is carried out in any other zone, and no picker may pick from bulk locations in Zone B or Zone E.

2. Picking may start only after PR-03 replenishment for that shift has been verified complete by the shift supervisor. Picking is assigned per shift — morning 06:00-14:00 and afternoon 14:00-22:00 — and pickers must not start a task in an aisle not yet released. Any face flagged as unavailable in the WMS is not to be picked until replenished.

3. Only the 10 pickers, and floaters trained and tasked as pickers for that shift, carry out order picking in Zone C. Pickers work exclusively against WMS tasks on the 20 handheld scanners. Paper pick lists, verbal instructions or memory picking are not permitted. Forklift operators do not pick orders and pickers do not drive counterbalance forklifts or reach trucks.

4. The WMS generates PR-04 tasks from released outbound orders, allocating SKU, quantity, batch or lot and expiry where applicable, and sequence by location walk in Zone C. Tasks are assigned to a named picker on the scanner; a picker may work only the task and locations displayed on their device. Split tasks or reassignment require shift supervisor instruction in the WMS.

5. At each pick face the picker must scan the location label first, then scan each item or carton barcode as it is picked, then confirm quantity. The scanner enforces FIFO by expiry or batch as allocated and rejects wrong SKU, wrong batch or wrong quantity. No item may be placed in the tote, cart or pallet without a successful scan; scan-verification before packing is mandatory for every item.

6. Pickers observe standard disciplines in the aisles: 3.0 m rack-storage aisles in Zone C and 4.0 m main transport aisles remain clear, 1.2 m yellow-barrier walkways are not used for staging, and 10 km/h building speed and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones and crossings apply to pallet jacks and carts. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory on the floor. Damaged cartons, loose goods or seal failures found in the face are not picked and are reported immediately.

7. Shortages, damage or discrepancies in the face are handled as PR-04 exceptions in Zone C. The picker logs a short-pick or damage flag on the scanner with location, SKU and quantity, leaves the face as found, and moves to the next task location. The shift supervisor and stock controller are notified; the face is not corrected by adjustment without a second count under PR-08, and damaged goods are transferred to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

8. Once scan-verified, picked goods are placed as instructed for the order — per tote, carton or pallet — and moved to the packing and labelling point for Zone C before transfer to Zone D. Every picked item must be scan-verified before it is packed; no unpacked or unverified item may be moved to Zone D. Labels are applied only after verification, and wrapped pallets only are staged in Zone D.

9. Completion is closed on the scanner by the picker with quantity, time and name, and the WMS updates order and inventory status only on these scans. The shift supervisor monitors progress on the WMS, reassigns tasks to meet the dispatcher release plan, and records completion and exceptions in the PR-04 log for PR-15 handover. No order is presented as picked or available for dispatch until all its PR-04 scans are complete.

title: Scan Verification
text:
1. Scan verification is the mandatory control under PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling that links picking in Zone C to packing and transfer to Zone D. Every item picked from a ground-level pick face or flow rack in Zone C must be scan-verified before it is packed, before a label is applied, and before it leaves Zone C. No unchecked, un-scanned or manually counted item may be packed or moved to Zone D.

2. Verification is carried out only by the assigned picker using one of the 20 handheld WMS scanners against the live PR-04 task. The picker must scan the location label first, then scan the item or carton barcode, then confirm quantity on the scanner. The sequence is fixed: location, item, quantity. Packing must not start until all three scans for that pick line have succeeded.

3. The WMS enforces the check at scan. It accepts only the SKU, batch or lot, expiry and quantity allocated for that order and location, in FIFO order where applicable. A wrong SKU, wrong batch, wrong expiry or wrong quantity is rejected by the scanner with an audible and visual error, and the item must not be packed. Override, manual keying or packing on assumption is prohibited.

4. Where an order requires multiple units, each unit or each sealed carton is scanned individually as displayed on the task. A single scan for a multi-unit line is not valid. The scanner displays running count versus required count; the line is closed only when scanned quantity equals required quantity. The picker must not substitute variants, split packs or combine batches to meet quantity.

5. Exceptions found at verification are handled in Zone C without packing. Any shortage, damage, seal failure, label mismatch or scanner rejection is logged on the scanner as a PR-04 exception with location, SKU, quantity and reason. The affected item is not packed, the face is left as found, and the shift supervisor and stock controller are notified. Damaged goods are transferred to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09 and are not returned to the face.

6. Only after all scans for a line are accepted does the scanner release the line for packing. Packing and labelling takes place at the designated packing point for Zone C. The picker, or packing staff where tasked, packs the scan-verified goods into the instructed tote, carton or pallet, applies the WMS-generated order and handling label, and scan-verifies the label to the order. No label may be applied before its lines are verified and no packed unit may be closed without label scan.

7. The WMS updates inventory and order status only on scans: face quantity on location and item scan, packed status on label scan. No paper record, verbal confirmation or post-packing check replaces the scan. If a scanner fails, the picker stops the task, reports to the shift supervisor, obtains a replacement device, and re-scans the line; goods in doubt remain unpacked in Zone C until re-verified.

8. The shift supervisor owns compliance with scan verification on each shift. The supervisor monitors scanner exception rates, ensures pickers do not pick ahead of replenishment, verifies that no unpacked or unverified goods are moved to Zone D, and logs all PR-04 and PR-05 exceptions for PR-15 handover. Stock controllers carry out second counts under PR-08 where verification reveals stock discrepancy before any adjustment is posted.

9. Only scan-verified, packed and labelled goods may be transferred from Zone C to Zone D for wrapping and staging. Transfer is by the 4.0 m transport aisles with movement recorded by handover scan. Any tote, carton or pallet arriving in Zone D without a verified label scan is treated as non-compliant, is held and returned to Zone C for re-verification, and is not staged for dispatch at Doors 5-8.

title: Packing, Labelling and Wrapping in Zone D
text:
### ops.ch07.s1 Packing, Labelling and Wrapping in Zone D

1. Packing, labelling and wrapping for outbound is governed by PR-05 Packing and labelling and takes place only in Zone D in front of Doors 5-8. Zone D covers 900 m2 and is used solely for final packing completion, labelling, wrapping and outbound staging. No inbound, bulk storage or picking activity may take place in Zone D.

2. Only scan-verified goods transferred from Zone C may enter Zone D for PR-05. Every tote, carton or pallet arriving from Zone C must have its PR-04 location, item and quantity scans complete and its order label scan-verified. Any unit arriving without a verified label scan is held, not staged, and returned to Zone C for re-verification.

3. Packing in Zone D is completion of the order pack started at Zone C. Staff place scan-verified items into the instructed outer carton, tote or onto the outbound pallet as shown on the WMS task, observing quantity, batch or lot and expiry. No substitution of SKU, batch or pack size is permitted, and manual counting without a scanner is not permitted.

4. Labelling is applied only after all lines for the handling unit are scan-verified. The WMS generates the order, carton or pallet licence label showing client, order number, SKU, quantity, batch or lot and handling marks. The operator applies the label and scan-verifies label to order on one of the 20 handheld scanners. An unverified or mismatched label must not be closed and must not proceed to wrapping.

5. Wrapping is carried out in Zone D on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers shared by dispatch. Only trained operators may operate the wrappers. Every outbound pallet, load included, must be wrapped to a stable, contained load within the site limit of 900 kg per pallet, with labels outward facing and scannable. No unwrapped, partially wrapped or unstable pallet may be staged in Zone D or presented at Doors 5-8.

6. Goods requiring chilled handling and moved via Zone E, and goods from Zone F value-added packing where applicable, follow the same PR-05 gate: count, inspection, booking and scan verification before transfer to Zone D for labelling and wrapping. Damaged cartons, wet, crushed or seal-failed goods found during packing are not wrapped and are transferred to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

7. Zone discipline and safety apply throughout PR-05. Transport aisles of 4.0 m feeding Zone D and the 1.2 m yellow-barrier walkways and dock crossings must be kept clear; no packing waste, empty pallets or film may obstruct aisles, doors or levellers. Building speed is 10 km/h and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, and high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the floor in Zone D.

8. Only wrapped and labelled pallets that have passed PR-05 may be staged in Zone D. Staging is in marked outbound lanes by assigned door and load, with pallet IDs, door number, carrier and time recorded. Staging does not constitute release; pallets remain under Zone D control until released by the dispatcher under PR-06 for loading at Doors 5-8.

9. The PR-05 scan history — item scans from Zone C, label verification and wrapping confirmation with name, time and pallet ID — forms the audit trail for dispatch. The shift supervisor verifies PR-05 completion each shift, clears exceptions, and hands over staged, wrapped pallets and any held units in the PR-15 handover. No pallet may be loaded at Doors 5-8 unless PR-05 is complete and recorded.

title: Staging and Load Release
text:
### ops.ch07.s2 Staging and Load Release

1. Staging and load release in Zone D is governed by PR-06 Outbound dispatch and is owned by the dispatcher. Zone D covers 900 m2 in front of outbound Doors 5-8 and is used solely for outbound staging and loading. No pallet may be staged in Zone D and no vehicle may be loaded at Doors 5-8 without dispatcher release recorded in the dock schedule.

2. Only wrapped and labelled pallets that have completed PR-05 may be staged in Zone D. This means goods transferred from Zone C with all PR-04 scans complete, packed and label scan-verified on a handheld WMS scanner, and wrapped to a stable load on one of the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers. Every pallet staged must be within the site limit of 900 kg, load included, with labels outward facing and scannable; unwrapped, partially wrapped, unstable or unverified pallets must not be staged and must be held for correction.

3. Staging is in marked outbound lanes in Zone D by assigned door, carrier, load and time slot. Pallets are placed only in the lane for their released load and stacked only as single pallets on the floor, never block-stacked above floor level in Zone D. Lanes must not obstruct the 4.0 m main transport aisles, the 1.2 m yellow-barrier walkways or the marked pedestrian crossings at the dock ramps, and no staging may take place outside Zone D.

4. The dispatcher controls the outbound plan for Zone D. The dispatcher books transport, issues each carrier a specific door from Doors 5-8 at 1.2 m dock height and a time slot, and sequences arrivals to match staging capacity in Zone D. Floor staff, forklift operators and shift supervisors must not redirect a vehicle to a different door, swap lanes or change sequence without dispatcher re-authorisation in the WMS.

5. No load is released until the dispatcher confirms readiness: all pallets for the load are wrapped and labelled and staged in Zone D, the WMS shows the order as packed and complete, pallet IDs and quantities match the load manifest, and the assigned vehicle is booked for that door and slot. Release is recorded with door number, carrier, pallet IDs, name, time and signature; verbal release is not valid and staging alone does not constitute release.

6. Outbound capacity is fixed by the door structure. Doors 5-8 are outbound only and each handles 4 trailer loads per shift, giving 16 trailer loads per shift across Zone D. With contracted curtain-side trailers carrying 26,000 kg on 33 floor positions, a trailer takes 28 full-weight pallets at 900 kg each, which makes 448 full-weight pallets per shift the most that can be promised. The dispatcher must not schedule beyond this limit, and the shift supervisor must not stage beyond the marked lane capacity for that shift.

7. Loading takes place only after dispatcher release for that door. The vehicle must be correctly positioned, braked and chocked at the assigned door before its leveller is deployed, and levellers are operated only by trained Harborwick staff after confirmation by the shift supervisor. Forklift operators move wrapped pallets by the 4.0 m transport aisles using the 3.0 t counterbalance forklifts, electric pallet jacks or hand pallet jacks, scan-verify each pallet on departure from staging and on loading, and observe 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps.

8. Drivers remain under yard discipline during staging and release. Drivers report to the marked waiting area in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard on arrival and are called forward to Doors 5-8 only on dispatcher instruction via one-way circulation. Drivers must not enter the hall, walk in transport aisles or wait on ramps or levellers, and must use the 1.2 m walkways and crossings when moving between cab and trailer. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain mandatory for all staff on the floor in Zone D throughout staging and loading.

9. The PR-06 record — staged pallet IDs by door and load, dispatcher release, loading scans, carrier, seal number, name and time — with the PR-05 wrap and label history forms the outbound audit trail and is handed over under PR-15. Any shortage, damage, label mismatch or vehicle exception found at staging or loading is held in Zone D, not loaded, and reported to the shift supervisor and dispatcher for re-allocation; damaged goods are transferred to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09 and are not re-staged until disposition is approved.

title: Vehicle Loads and Outbound Capacity
text:
### ops.ch07.s3 Vehicle Loads and Outbound Capacity

1. Vehicle loads and outbound capacity in Zone D are controlled under PR-06 Outbound dispatch and are built on the single site standard that a pallet, load included, may weigh at most 900 kg. All vehicle weight limits, floor-position limits and shift promises in this section are calculated from this 900 kg pallet limit.

2. No pallet presented for loading at Doors 5-8 may exceed 900 kg. Pallets over 900 kg are non-compliant for outbound, must be held in Zone D, and must be reworked or split before release. Pallet weight as shown on the WMS pallet licence is the controlling figure for vehicle loading and must match the manifest.

3. The contracted curtain-side trailer is rated at 26,000 kg total payload and 33 floor positions. By weight it can carry 28 full-weight pallets at 900 kg each. Positions do not increase the weight allowance: a trailer loaded with 28 pallets at 900 kg is at its maximum weight even though 5 floor positions remain empty. Only where the average pallet weight is below 900 kg may more than 28 pallets be loaded, and then only up to 33 positions and never above 26,000 kg total.

4. The delivery van is rated at 1,800 kg and 6 floor positions. At the site limit this is two full-weight pallets at 900 kg each. Anything requiring more than two full-weight pallets, or any single load over 1,800 kg, must go by trailer and must not be assigned to the van.

5. Weight governs before positions for every load. Load planning must check total weight first, then positions, then door and lane availability. A load that would exceed 26,000 kg on a trailer or 1,800 kg on a van, or that places more than 33 pallets on a trailer or more than 6 handling units in a van, must be split into a second load and sequenced as a separate time slot by the dispatcher.

6. Outbound throughput is fixed by the door structure. Doors 5-8 are outbound only, each equipped with its own leveller at 1.2 m dock height, and each handles 4 trailer loads per shift. This gives 16 trailer loads per shift across Zone D. At 28 full-weight pallets per trailer, the maximum that can be promised to a client is 448 full-weight pallets per shift.

7. The 448-pallet figure is a per-shift ceiling for the operating window of 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus authorised Saturday morning overtime where approved. It is owned by the dispatcher for planning and by the shift supervisor for execution. The dispatcher must not book beyond 16 trailer loads per shift, and the supervisor must not stage or release beyond the marked lane capacity that supports that rate.

8. Every load is released only against a manifest showing pallet IDs, individual pallet weights, total weight, total positions and assigned door. Forklift operators load by that manifest via the 4.0 m transport aisles, scan-verify each pallet on departure from staging and on loading, and observe even weight distribution and no overhang beyond the trailer bed. The carrier's gross weight remains the carrier's legal responsibility, but no Harborwick load may be dispatched that exceeds the limits in this section.

9. Any exception — overweight pallet, overweight total, incomplete labelling, damaged or unwrapped pallet, or vehicle not matching the booked trailer or van type — stops loading for that door. The pallets are held in Zone D, the dispatcher and shift supervisor are notified, and the load is re-planned. No overweight or unverified pallet may be loaded to meet a slot, and no slot may be split across doors to avoid the per-vehicle limits.

title: Aisle Network and Walkways
text:
1. The internal transport and pedestrian network is fixed by the hall layout and is governed by PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. All movement inside the building takes place on defined aisles and walkways; no person and no truck may create an informal route through storage, staging or racking areas.

2. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. They form the primary circulation spine connecting Zones A to F and the eight dock doors to bulk storage, picking and dispatch. Only forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks may travel in these aisles, and the aisles must be kept completely clear of pallets, empty pallet stacks, film, waste and idle MHE at all times.

3. Rack-storage aisles between rack rows are 3.0 m wide. They provide access to rack bays in Zone B and to pick faces and flow racks in Zone C. Goods must remain within the rack beam envelope and must not protrude into the 3.0 m aisle, and no staging or parking of trucks is permitted inside these aisles.

4. Pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide and are physically separated from all vehicle routes by continuous yellow barriers. The walkways are the only permitted pedestrian routes on the warehouse floor and in the dock approaches, and they connect the office annex personnel doors to Zones A to F and to the yard crossing points. Walking outside the barriers in any transport or storage aisle is not permitted.

5. Separation is physical and continuous. Yellow barriers run the full length of the walkways, around pedestrian zones and alongside dock ramps, with marked crossings where a walkway must cross a transport aisle. Barriers must not be removed, moved or bridged by pallets, and any damaged barrier is reported to the shift supervisor and maintenance technician and the route taken out of use until repaired.

6. Every crossing between a 1.2 m walkway and a 4.0 m or 3.0 m aisle is permanently marked on the floor with zebra hatching and signage. Pedestrians must stop at the barrier gate, check both directions and cross only when clear, and must not loiter on the crossing. MHE must give way at every marked crossing and must not overtake or queue across a crossing.

7. At the docks, pedestrian and vehicle movements are fully segregated. The walkways provide the only access to the door areas at Doors 1-4 inbound and Doors 5-8 outbound, with marked crossings at each ramp and leveller at 1.2 m dock height. Drivers on foot moving between cab and trailer must use the walkways and crossings, and warehouse staff must not walk on ramps or behind reversing vehicles.

8. No storage, staging or work activity may take place on or over the walkways. Pallets, totes, packing waste, chargers, stretch film and empty hand pallet jacks must not be placed within the 1.2 m width or against the barriers, and overhanging loads in adjacent aisles must not intrude over the barrier line. The 10 m clear height is maintained above main transport aisles and must not be reduced by fixtures that obscure walkway sightlines.

9. The shift supervisor owns compliance with the aisle and walkway discipline on every shift. The supervisor ensures 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and 1.2 m walkways are clear, barriers and markings intact, crossings visible and unobstructed, and that all staff and authorised visitors use only the designated walkways. Non-compliance is stopped immediately and logged for review under PR-11 and PR-15.

title: Speed Limits
text:
### ops.ch08.s2 Speed Limits

1. Speed limits at Harborwick 3PL are fixed site limits and apply on every shift, including peak-season overtime. Three limits cover all vehicle movement inside the hall and in the fenced yard. No supervisor, dispatcher or driver may authorise an exception, and no operational pressure justifies exceeding them.

2. Inside the building the limit is 10 km/h. This applies to all powered MHE — the 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, the 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t, and the 11 electric pallet jacks — as well as any other vehicle or towed load from the moment it passes the dock door threshold. The 10 km/h limit covers the 4.0 m main transport aisles, the 3.0 m rack-storage aisles in Zones B and C, and all movement in Zones A to F within the hall.

3. In the fenced yard of approximately 3,500 m2 the limit is 12 km/h. This applies to all inbound and outbound carriers, yard shunters where used, and any Harborwick MHE operating outside the hall. Yard circulation is one-way to and from the dock ramps, and the 12 km/h limit applies on all yard lanes, queuing approaches and waiting-area approaches at all times.

4. Wherever people and trucks can meet the limit is 5 km/h and this limit always overrides the others. The 5 km/h zone covers every marked pedestrian zone, every marked crossing between the 1.2 m yellow-barrier walkways and a 4.0 m or 3.0 m aisle, and every dock ramp and leveller area at the eight doors at 1.2 m dock height. At these locations MHE must slow to walking pace, give way at crossings, and be prepared to stop.

5. Limits are posted on permanent signage at hall entrances, yard gates, aisle entries and each dock ramp, supported by floor markings at crossings and pedestrian zones. Posted speed is the maximum, not the target; operators must drive slower whenever load, visibility, aisle width, congestion or floor condition requires it. Loaded trucks, high lifts and cornering always require below-limit speed.

6. The limits apply to every driver without exception: forklift operators, inbound operators using pallet jacks, pickers and floaters moving hand pallet jacks, the maintenance technician, and visiting drivers on foot or in cabs while in the yard. Reversing on dock ramps, approaching levellers, and moving with restricted forward view must be at 5 km/h or less, with audible warning and observation at barriers.

7. No load, schedule or dock slot justifies speed. Operators must keep the load stable, forks or pallet low while travelling, and maintain clear sightlines over and around the load and racking. If visibility is blocked, the operator must stop, reposition or seek banksman guidance and must not proceed at 10 km/h on assumption that the aisle is clear.

8. The shift supervisor on duty owns enforcement on the floor and at the docks, and the dispatcher owns call-forward pacing that prevents bunching in the yard. Any breach, near-miss or contact linked to speed is stopped immediately, the MHE or vehicle grounded where required, and the incident logged for review under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Repeated or serious breaches are escalated to the warehouse manager for re-authorisation.

9. Speed compliance forms part of the PR-15 End-of-Shift Handover. The outgoing supervisor records any speeding observation, crossing or ramp incursion, damaged signage or barrier, or MHE grounded after a speed-related event, and the incoming supervisor verifies that signage, markings and barriers are visible and unobstructed before operations restart.

title: Pedestrian Safety Rules
text:
### ops.ch08.s3 Pedestrian Safety Rules

1. Pedestrian safety on the warehouse floor and at the docks is governed by PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. PR-11 applies to every person in the hall and on the dock approaches on all shifts, including peak-season overtime, and is enforced by the shift supervisor on duty.

2. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, no exceptions. This includes all Harborwick staff, managers, maintenance and office staff entering the hall, drivers on foot when authorised, and visitors. No person may enter or remain on the floor, in Zones A to F, or in the dock walkway areas without a fastened high-visibility vest.

3. Class S3 safety footwear is mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, no exceptions. Trainers, low shoes or any footwear below S3 standard is not permitted beyond the office annex personnel doors. Staff without compliant footwear must not be assigned floor tasks and must leave the floor until compliant.

4. Pedestrians may walk only on the designated 1.2 m walkways physically separated by continuous yellow barriers. Walking in 4.0 m main transport aisles, in 3.0 m rack-storage aisles, on dock ramps or levellers at 1.2 m dock height, or through storage and staging areas is prohibited. Barriers must not be removed, climbed, bridged with pallets or blocked, and any damage is reported to the shift supervisor immediately.

5. Every crossing between a walkway and a vehicle aisle or dock ramp is permanently marked with zebra hatching, signage and barrier gates. Pedestrians must stop at the gate, make eye contact with the operator where possible, check both directions, and cross only when clear.
