9. Completed incident reports and corrective actions are filed for audit and tracked to completion. The maintenance technician retains repair logs, the shift supervisor retains the file of reviewed reports, and stock controllers retain any related cycle count and adjustment records where inventory was affected. No stock adjustment is posted without a second count under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.

10. Any open incident, cordoned area, tagged-out truck or pending corrective action is handed over at end of shift under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. The incoming shift supervisor must confirm receipt, verify that controls remain in place, and brief floor staff before work resumes.

chapter_title: Chapter 4 - Incidents, Damage and Emergency Response
title: 4.2 Damaged Goods, Quarantine and Returns
text:
### hs.ch04.s2 4.2 Damaged Goods, Quarantine and Returns

1. All damaged, suspected damaged and suspected non-conforming goods anywhere on site must be treated as unsafe for sale and removed from the normal flow immediately. This applies to damage found during receiving in Zone A, put-away and storage in Zone B, picking in Zone C, dispatch in Zone D, cold storage in Zone E and services activity in Zone F, including damage from rack strikes, drops, forklift impacts, leaks, water ingress, crushed packaging and failed cold-chain.

2. Damaged goods go to quarantine the same day they are found. The discovering employee must stop handling the unit, protect it from further damage, warn others if there is a spill or sharp hazard, inform the shift supervisor in charge of the floor immediately and move the goods to quarantine in Zone F before the end of the shift. Goods must not be returned to racking, block stacking, pick faces or outbound staging and must not be dispatched.

3. Quarantine is located only in Zone F, the 600 m2 services and control zone. No other zone may hold damaged goods overnight. Each quarantined pallet or unit must be labelled with date, time, zone found, WMS reference, reason and finder, and booked by WMS movement to quarantine under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. The shift supervisor verifies the booking and ensures the quarantine area remains segregated and clear of through traffic.

4. Damaged chilled goods from Zone E must be moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day and identified as cold-chain break. They must not be returned to +2 °C to +6 °C storage. Damaged hazmat packages must where safe to do so be moved to quarantine inside the ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2 in Zone F the same day; if movement would increase risk of leak, fire or exposure the goods must be isolated in place, the area cordoned off and PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response followed before any transfer.

5. No stock adjustment, write-off or rework is posted on the basis of damage alone. Stock controllers carry out a second count to confirm quantity and identity under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, and only then propose an adjustment. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count.

6. Approval thresholds for damaged-goods write-offs are fixed. The shift supervisor may approve write-offs up to 750 EUR. Any write-off above 750 EUR must be approved and signed off by the Warehouse Manager, who is also accountable for sign-off of the annual wall-to-wall stocktake. Verbal approvals are not permitted and goods remain in quarantine until written approval is recorded.

7. Returns are handled only through Zone F and only under PR-07 Returns handling. Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery. Returns staff inspect every unit returned, check identity, quantity, packaging, seals, temperature history for cold goods and damage, and record the result with WMS references and photos where required.

8. After inspection returns staff propose a single disposition for each unit: restock to Zone B, E or F, rework under instruction, or scrap. No returned goods may be restocked without inspection and booking. Rework and restock must meet product and client specifications; any doubt is treated as scrap. Cold-chain returns that have left controlled conditions and any hazmat return with compromised containment must not be restocked without explicit assessment.

9. Final disposition of inspected returns is approved only by the shift supervisor. Staff may not release restock, rework or scrap until the shift supervisor has reviewed the inspection and signed the decision. Approved restock is booked back to the assigned zone by WMS task; approved scrap is held segregated pending write-off and safe disposal under PR-09.

10. Every quarantine movement, second count, inspection and disposition is logged and retained for audit. Any open quarantine, pending second count or pending write-off approval is handed over at end of shift under PR-15 End-of-shift handover, and linked incidents are reported and reviewed under the incident process in 4.1.

chapter_title: Chapter 4 - Incidents, Damage and Emergency Response
title: 4.3 Evacuation, Alarms and Drills
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL maintains a single evacuation system for the entire 6,000 m2 hall covering Zones A to F, the office annex and the 3,500 m2 fenced yard. On activation of the fire alarm, evacuation alarm or on instruction under PR-14 Emergency evacuation, all work stops immediately. Forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks must be stopped safely, forks lowered and power secured where time permits, and must never block the 4.0 m main transport aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles or 1.2 m pedestrian walkways used as escape routes.

2. All personnel inside the fence, including employees, visitors, contractors and drivers in the marked waiting area, must evacuate via the nearest safe pedestrian walkway and emergency exit to the assembly point by the north fence. Yellow-barrier walkways and marked crossings provide the protected routes; running, use of trucks to exit, and re-entry to collect personal items are prohibited.

3. The shift supervisor in charge of the floor is in control of every evacuation. On any alarm the shift supervisor takes command, orders evacuation, ensures levellers and roller doors are left safe, directs floor staff to sweep Zones A to F including Zone E cold zone and Zone F hazmat cage and quarantine where safe to do so, and confirms the hall is cleared.

4. The shift supervisor accounts for all persons by roll call at the assembly point by the north fence. Roll call uses the shift roster, visitor and driver log from the dispatcher, and confirmation from zone sweepers. No zone is assumed clear without positive confirmation.

5. Roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building. No person may leave the assembly point or re-enter the hall, yard work area or office annex until the shift supervisor has completed the roll call, accounted for every person, and given explicit clearance. Missing persons are reported immediately to emergency services by the shift supervisor.

6. The shift supervisor liaises with emergency services on arrival, provides site information including hazmat cage location and quantity up to 4,000 kg, cold zone status and any cordoned racking or tagged-out trucks, and controls the perimeter until handover to emergency services or the Warehouse Manager where present.

7. Re-entry is authorised only by the shift supervisor after alarms are silenced, the cause is investigated and the building is declared safe; or by emergency services where they have taken control. The shift supervisor records time of all-clear and briefs staff before work resumes. Any damage to racking, barriers, doors, alarms or refrigeration is reported to the maintenance technician for immediate logging and repair.

8. An evacuation drill is run every quarter under PR-14. Each drill tests alarm activation, evacuation via walkways and exits, sweep of all six zones, roll call at the north fence assembly point and the no re-entry rule. Drills are scheduled to cover both shifts 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and any authorised Saturday overtime so that all staff participate over the year.

9. Every drill and every real evacuation is documented. The shift supervisor records date, time, zones involved, persons present, time to clear the hall, time to complete roll call, deficiencies found and corrective actions, and retains the record for audit. Corrective actions include retraining, repair of exits, signage, barriers and alarms, and updates to PR-14.

10. Any open evacuation issue, failed alarm, blocked exit or pending repair is handed over at end of shift under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. The incoming shift supervisor must confirm receipt, verify that exits, walkways and assembly point access remain clear, and brief floor staff. The Warehouse Manager is accountable for ensuring quarterly drills are completed and that supervision and equipment are in place on every shift.

title: 1.1 Warehouse Manager - Site Accountability and Final Sign-offs
text:
### roles.ch01.s1 1.1 Warehouse Manager - Site Accountability and Final Sign-offs

1. The Warehouse Manager is the single accountable owner of Harborwick 3PL Ltd. site in Port Sellow. The role is accountable for all operations, safety, compliance and inventory integrity across the 6,000 m2 hall, the 3,500 m2 fenced yard and all six zones (A-F), across both shifts Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and any authorised Saturday overtime.

2. The Warehouse Manager exercises overall control of site activities. This includes inbound receiving through doors 1-4, bulk storage in Zone B, picking in Zone C, dispatch through doors 5-8, cold storage in Zone E and all service functions in Zone F including the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage. No activity may override the site rules on zone separation, dock-door directionality or capacity limits.

3. The following authorisations are reserved to the Warehouse Manager only and may not be delegated:
a) authorisation of any new forklift operator to operate MHE. No licence, no truck - authorisation is personal and documented;
b) approval of all overtime, including peak-season Saturday morning overtime;
c) final sign-off of the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results;
d) approval of any damaged-goods write-off above 750 EUR. Write-offs up to and including 750 EUR are approved by the Shift Supervisor.

4. The Warehouse Manager is accountable for staffing and organisation of approximately 38-40 personnel, including 2 Shift Supervisors, 2 Dispatchers, 2 Stock Controllers and all operational staff. The Manager assigns accountability to the Shift Supervisor on duty for floor leadership and incident response on each shift, while retaining overall accountability.

5. The Warehouse Manager is accountable for adherence to physical and operational limits. These include a maximum pallet weight of 900 kg, a maximum of 2,700 kg per rack bay, block-stacking limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m, a maximum of 4,000 kg (4 full-weight pallets) in the hazmat cage at any time, and outbound capacity planning of 416 full-weight pallets per shift (4 outbound doors x 4 trailer loads).

6. The Warehouse Manager owns safety governance. The role ensures enforcement of speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, maintenance of 1.2 m physically separated pedestrian walkways, and mandatory wearing of high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the warehouse floor and seat belts for moving forklift operators.

7. The Warehouse Manager is responsible for the periodic control regime. This includes ensuring that cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule, that no inventory adjustment is posted without a second count, that racking receives a documented safety inspection every month, and that an evacuation drill with roll call at the north fence assembly point is conducted every quarter before re-entry.

8. The Warehouse Manager owns the fifteen site procedures PR-01 to PR-15 and ensures they are applied as written: PR-01 Inbound receiving, PR-02 Put-away, PR-03 Replenishment, PR-04 Order picking, PR-05 Packing and labelling, PR-06 Outbound dispatch, PR-07 Returns handling, PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, PR-11 Pedestrian safety, PR-12 Cold-chain handling, PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response, PR-14 Emergency evacuation, PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Where a procedure conflicts with this brief, the brief prevails.

9. The Warehouse Manager ensures that all equipment checks, temperature verifications for Zone E (+2 °C to +6 °C), hazmat controls and incident reviews are completed and logged, and that any issue affecting accuracy, safety or client service is escalated and closed under the Manager's authority.

title: 1.2 Shift Supervisor - Shift Leadership and Incident Ownership
text:
### roles.ch01.s2 1.2 Shift Supervisor - Shift Leadership and Incident Ownership

1. The Shift Supervisor is the designated leader of the warehouse floor for each shift. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. operates two shifts Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, with authorised Saturday morning overtime in peak season. One Shift Supervisor is in charge of the floor at all times, with two Shift Supervisors covering the roster. Accountability for the shift rests with the supervisor on duty.

2. The Shift Supervisor directs all floor staff present on the shift, including forklift operators, inbound operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns and packing staff, floaters and the maintenance technician as required. The dispatcher retains ownership of dock scheduling and carrier allocation to doors 1-4 inbound and 5-8 outbound; the Shift Supervisor ensures the floor executes those assignments and that drivers remain in the marked waiting area and do not enter the hall.

3. The Shift Supervisor enforces zone discipline and operational sequence on the shift:
a) no goods move past Zone A until documents are checked and goods are inspected and booked;
b) put-away is directed only to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F as instructed;
c) replenishment of Zone C pick faces is completed before each picking shift;
d) only wrapped and labelled pallets are staged in Zone D for the assigned outbound door.

4. The Shift Supervisor ensures that physical and capacity limits are observed on the shift. This includes the maximum pallet weight of 900 kg, a maximum of 2,700 kg per rack bay, block-stacking limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m, and a maximum of 4,000 kg (4 full-weight pallets) in the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F. Hazmat is stored only in the cage. Any breach is stopped, quarantined and escalated to the Warehouse Manager.

5. The Shift Supervisor is responsible for safety compliance on the shift. This includes enforcement of speed limits of 8 km/h inside the building, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, use of the 1.2 m physically separated pedestrian walkways with yellow barriers, and mandatory wearing of high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the warehouse floor and seat belts by forklift operators when moving. The supervisor ensures every truck receives its documented check before first use that day.

6. The Shift Supervisor owns incident response on the shift. The role acts as first responder, secures the area, ensures first aid and emergency services are called where required, initiates evacuation under PR-14 where necessary and conducts roll call at the assembly point by the north fence before anyone re-enters. Every incident on the shift is documented and reviewed by the Shift Supervisor, with corrective actions tracked and escalated to the Warehouse Manager.

7. The Shift Supervisor holds the following approval authorities on the shift, within limits set by the Warehouse Manager:
a) approval of damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 750 EUR under PR-09. Any write-off above 750 EUR requires approval by the Warehouse Manager;
b) final disposition of inspected returns under PR-07 (restock, rework or scrap) following inspection in Zone F;
c) review and sign-off of every incident report arising on the shift.

8. The Shift Supervisor does not hold authorities reserved to the Warehouse Manager: authorisation of new forklift operators to operate MHE, approval of overtime, and final sign-off of the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results. Requests requiring those authorisations are escalated.

9. The Shift Supervisor ensures compliance with the site procedures relevant to shift execution, including PR-01 Inbound receiving, PR-02 Put-away, PR-03 Replenishment, PR-04 Order picking, PR-06 Outbound dispatch, PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, PR-11 Pedestrian safety, PR-12 Cold-chain handling manual verification each shift for Zone E +2 °C to +6 °C, PR-13 Hazmat handling, PR-14 Emergency evacuation and PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Where a procedure conflicts with the owner brief, the brief prevails.

10. The Shift Supervisor conducts a documented end-of-shift handover to the incoming supervisor under PR-15, covering open inbound and outbound loads, staffing and equipment status, cold-chain and hazmat status, incidents and quarantine, and any delayed tasks. All outstanding risks are explicitly handed over or escalated to the Warehouse Manager.

title: 1.3 Dispatcher - Transport Booking and Dock Scheduling
text:
### roles.ch01.s3 1.3 Dispatcher - Transport Booking and Dock Scheduling

1. The Dispatcher is the owner of transport booking and dock scheduling for Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow. Two Dispatchers cover the operation across both shifts Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and any authorised Saturday morning peak overtime, ensuring continuous control of the 8 dock doors at 1.2 m height in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard.

2. The Dispatcher has sole authority to assign every carrier a dock door and a time slot. Doors 1-4 are inbound only and doors 5-8 are outbound only. No truck may approach a door without a Dispatcher-issued assignment, and no assignment may violate door directionality. The Dispatcher communicates assignments in advance and controls the marked driver waiting area; drivers wait there and never enter the hall.

3. For inbound transport, the Dispatcher books and schedules all arrivals to doors 1-4 on time slots that balance inspection capacity in Zone A and put-away capacity in Zone B, Zone E and Zone F. No unloading may start until documents are checked in Zone A under PR-01, and the Dispatcher reschedules any carrier that arrives outside its slot or without correct paperwork in coordination with the Shift Supervisor.

4. For outbound transport, the Dispatcher books and schedules all dispatches from doors 5-8. The Dispatcher plans outbound capacity on the basis of 4 outbound doors each handling 4 trailer loads per shift, which is a maximum of 416 full-weight pallets per shift. The Dispatcher does not promise capacity beyond this limit and escalates any request that would exceed it to the Warehouse Manager.

5. The Dispatcher applies the site load limits when booking transport. A pallet including load may weigh at most 1,000 kg. The contracted curtain-side trailer capacity is 26,000 kg on 33 floor positions, equating to 26 full-weight pallets per trailer. The delivery van capacity is 1,800 kg on 6 positions, equating to one full-weight pallet; any load heavier than 1,000 kg on a single pallet position or exceeding van limits is allocated to trailer transport only.

6. The Dispatcher releases outbound loads under PR-06. A load is released only when pallets are fully wrapped, labelled, scan-verified and staged in Zone D for the assigned outbound door. Only booked goods put away under PR-02 and picked and packed under PR-04 and PR-05 may be released. The Dispatcher confirms door, carrier, destination and load seal before authorising loading.

7. The Dispatcher maintains the dock schedule as the live control document for the yard and hall interface. This includes monitoring slot adherence, door occupancy, leveller availability and staging readiness in Zone D, and re-assigning doors and slots where delays, breakdowns or incidents occur. All changes are communicated immediately to the Shift Supervisor on duty and to affected carriers.

8. The Dispatcher ensures compliance with site procedures relevant to transport and dispatch, including PR-01 Inbound receiving, PR-06 Outbound dispatch and PR-15 End-of-shift handover. The Dispatcher logs every booking, door assignment, time slot, arrival and departure time and load release, and hands over open loads, delayed carriers and next-shift bookings to the incoming Dispatcher and the Shift Supervisor.

9. The Dispatcher does not hold authorities reserved to the Warehouse Manager or Shift Supervisor. The role does not authorise new forklift operators, does not approve overtime, does not approve damaged-goods write-offs and does not sign off stocktake results. Any hazmat movement requiring use of the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F is scheduled only within its 4,000 kg limit and in coordination with the Shift Supervisor under PR-13. Where a procedure conflicts with the owner brief, the brief prevails.

title: 2.1 Forklift Operator - MHE Operation and Load Limits
text:
### roles.ch02.s1 2.1 Forklift Operator - MHE Operation and Load Limits

1. The Forklift Operator is authorised to operate materials handling equipment (MHE) at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow. The role works across the 6,000 m2 hall and the 3,500 m2 fenced yard on shifts Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and any authorised Saturday morning peak overtime, under direction of the Shift Supervisor on duty.

2. The Forklift Operator may operate only the equipment for which they are personally authorised. The site fleet comprises 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t for general work, 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t for the high bays in Zone B, 11 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks for small moves. No other MHE is operated by this role.

3. No person may operate any truck without authorisation. Only the Warehouse Manager authorises new forklift operators to operate MHE; the principle "no licence, no truck" applies and authorisation is personal and documented. The Forklift Operator does not authorise others, does not approve overtime and does not sign off stocktakes or write-offs.

4. The Forklift Operator performs all MHE movements required by the operation. This includes put-away from Zone A to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F under PR-02, replenishment of pick faces in Zone C from bulk storage under PR-03, movements to and from Zone D dispatch staging and Zone F services, and any repositioning directed by the Shift Supervisor. No goods are moved past Zone A until documents are checked and goods are inspected and booked.

5. The Forklift Operator operates strictly within site load and storage limits:
a) a pallet including load may weigh at most 1,000 kg;
b) each rack bay in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg;
c) free block-stacking elsewhere is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m;
d) the ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F of 60 m2 holds at most 4,000 kg at any time, equating to 4 full-weight pallets, and hazmat is stored only in the cage.
Any load exceeding limits is stopped, grounded and reported immediately to the Shift Supervisor.

6. The Forklift Operator observes all speed and separation rules. Speed limits are 8 km/h inside the building, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet, including marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. The operator uses only designated transport aisles, which are 4.0 m wide for main aisles and 3.0 m for rack storage aisles, and gives way to pedestrians at all times. The 1.2 m pedestrian walkways physically separated by yellow barriers are never driven on or blocked.

7. A documented pre-use check is completed for every truck before its first use each day under PR-10 and logged as complete. The check covers brakes, steering, forks, mast chains, tyres, lights, horn, battery or charge state and safety devices. No truck with a defect affecting safety is used; defects are tagged, immobilised and reported to the Shift Supervisor and Maintenance Technician immediately.

8. The Forklift Operator complies with mandatory PPE and operating discipline. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are worn at all times on the warehouse floor without exception; seat belts are worn whenever the truck is moving. Dock levellers at the 8 doors at 1.2 m height are used only as instructed, and drivers remain in the marked waiting area and never enter the hall.

9. The Forklift Operator works in accordance with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse and where applicable PR-02 Put-away, PR-03 Replenishment, PR-12 Cold-chain handling for Zone E (+2 °C to +6 °C) and PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. Where a procedure conflicts with the owner brief, the brief prevails.

title: 2.2 Inbound Operator - Receiving, Inspection and Put-Away
text:
### roles.ch02.s2 2.2 Inbound Operator - Receiving, Inspection and Put-Away

1. The Inbound Operator is responsible for all receiving, inspection and put-away initiation activities in Zone A (800 m2) at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow. The role operates at inbound docks 1-4 at 1.2 m dock height and controls the flow of goods from vehicle arrival to transfer to storage, working Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and any authorised Saturday morning peak overtime under direction of the Shift Supervisor on duty.

2. The Inbound Operator executes the door and slot plan owned by the Dispatcher. No vehicle is approached without a Dispatcher-issued assignment to a specific inbound door and time slot, and doors 1-4 are inbound only. The Inbound Operator ensures drivers remain in the marked waiting area and never enter the hall, and uses the dock leveller only as instructed.

3. The Inbound Operator applies the strict document-first sequence under PR-01 Inbound receiving. On arrival at the assigned door, delivery documents are checked before any unloading begins. No goods move past Zone A until the paperwork is checked. Any discrepancy in documents, quantities, purchase order or carrier identity is stopped and escalated to the Shift Supervisor and Dispatcher before unloading.

4. Once documents are cleared, the Inbound Operator unloads, counts and inspects all goods in Zone A. This includes physical count against documents, inspection for visible damage, shortage, overage and labelling accuracy, and temperature check on arrival for goods destined for Zone E. Only inspected goods are booked into the WMS via the handheld scanner; only booked goods may go to put-away.

5. The Inbound Operator records every receipt accurately in the system. This includes supplier, product code, batch and expiry where applicable, quantity received, quantity damaged or rejected, and door and time. No manual adjustment or bypass of scan verification is permitted. All 20 handheld WMS scanners are shared resources and are returned and logged after use.

6. The Inbound Operator initiates transfer to storage zones under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Booked goods are labelled and directed to put-away in Zone B bulk storage (2,400 pallet positions), Zone E cold zone (300 m2, +2 °C to +6 °C) or Zone F services and hazmat cage (60 m2 ventilated) as instructed by the system and the Shift Supervisor. Replenishment of Zone C pick faces from bulk is not part of this role but put-away accuracy enables it.

7. The Inbound Operator observes all physical and operational limits applicable to Zone A and transfer. This includes a maximum pallet weight of 1,000 kg (trailer capacity 26,000 kg on 33 positions = 26 full-weight pallets; van capacity 1,800 kg on 6 positions = one full-weight pallet), a maximum of 2,700 kg per rack bay in Zone B, free block-stacking limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m where used, and hazmat stored only in the ventilated cage in Zone F with a maximum of 4,000 kg (4 full-weight pallets) at any time. Any overload or breach is grounded and reported immediately.

8. Damaged, suspect or non-conforming goods are handled under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Such goods are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, clearly identified and logged, and not returned to stock without Shift Supervisor decision. The Inbound Operator does not approve write-offs; write-offs up to 500 EUR are approved by the Shift Supervisor and above 500 EUR by the Warehouse Manager are replaced with: write-offs up to and including 750 EUR are approved by the Shift Supervisor and any write-off above 750 EUR by the Warehouse Manager.

9. The Inbound Operator complies with site safety and procedural controls. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory on the warehouse floor at all times; speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are observed, and the 1.2 m physically separated pedestrian walkways with yellow barriers are never blocked. The role operates only MHE for which it is personally authorised under PR-10 — only the Warehouse Manager authorises new forklift operators — and completes documented equipment checks before first use. Work is performed in accordance with PR-01, PR-02, PR-09, PR-11 Pedestrian safety, PR-12 Cold-chain handling and PR-13 Hazmat handling where applicable, and is handed over under PR-15. Where a procedure conflicts with the owner brief, the brief prevails.

title: 2.3 Picker - Replenishment, Picking and Handover to Dispatch
text:
### roles.ch02.s3 2.3 Picker - Replenishment, Picking and Handover to Dispatch

1. The Picker is responsible for replenishment verification, order picking and handover to dispatch in Zone C (1,200 m2) at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow. The role operates ground-level pick faces and flow racks fed from bulk storage, working Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and any authorised Saturday morning peak overtime under direction of the Shift Supervisor on duty.

2. The Picker works exclusively against WMS scanner tasks. No item is picked without an active scanner task on one of the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners, and every picked item is scan-verified before it is packed. Scanners are returned and logged after use, and no manual bypass of scan verification is permitted. Any shortfall, overage, damage or location error is reported immediately to the Shift Supervisor and Stock Controller and is not adjusted by the Picker.

3. The Picker ensures pick-face readiness before and during each picking shift under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces and PR-04 Order picking. Pick faces in Zone C are replenished from bulk storage in Zone B (2,400 pallet positions) before each picking shift. The Picker checks face quantities, expiry and batch sequence where applicable, requests replenishment where stock is low or absent, and does not pick from empty, damaged or unreplenished locations. Replenishment movements requiring counterbalance forklifts (3.0 t) or reach trucks (2.0 t) are executed only by authorised Forklift Operators.

4. Picking is performed in Zone C in strict location, product, batch and quantity sequence as directed by the scanner. The Picker observes FIFO and FEFO where instructed by the system, scans each unit, pack and outer as required, and segregates any damaged, mislabelled or suspect goods found on the face. Such goods are removed from the pick, clearly identified and notified for quarantine in Zone F under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling the same day they are found.

5. After scan verification, the Picker packs, labels and consolidates orders under PR-05 Packing and labelling. Every carton and pallet is labelled as instructed by the system, with correct customer, order and destination data. A pallet including load may weigh at most 1,000 kg, and the Picker does not build pallets beyond safe stacking or handling limits and reports any overload for correction by the Shift Supervisor.

6. The Picker moves completed, labelled pallets to Zone D (900 m2) for outbound staging under PR-04 and PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Only wrapped and labelled pallets are staged in Zone D in front of the assigned outbound dock 5-8. The Picker places pallets only in the staging lane for the door assigned by the Dispatcher and does not load trailers; loading and seal confirmation are controlled by the Dispatcher and Shift Supervisor.

7. Where the Picker is personally authorised to operate MHE, movements in Zone C and to Zone D may be made with hand pallet jacks and electric pallet jacks; counterbalance forklifts and reach trucks are operated only if the Picker holds separate personal authorisation from the Warehouse Manager under the principle "no licence, no truck". In all cases a documented pre-use check is completed before first use that day under PR-10, and defective equipment is tagged and reported.

8. The Picker complies with all site limits and safety controls applicable to Zone C and transfer routes. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory on the warehouse floor at all times without exception. Speed limits of 8 km/h inside the building, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are observed. The 1.2 m physically separated pedestrian walkways with yellow barriers are never blocked, and main transport aisles of 4.0 m and rack storage aisles of 3.0 m are kept clear.

9. The Picker operates in accordance with PR-03, PR-04, PR-05, PR-06, PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, PR-09, PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse and, where handling chilled goods, PR-12 Cold-chain handling (+2 °C to +6 °C) under supervisor instruction. The Picker does not approve write-offs, does not post inventory adjustments and does not sign off returns; returns handling in Zone F and cycle counts are owned by other roles. Work is handed over under PR-15 End-of-shift handover, including open tasks, shortages, equipment status and staging readiness. Where a procedure conflicts with the owner brief, the brief prevails.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Specialist Functions and Site-Wide Standards
title: 3.1 Stock Controller - Inventory Accuracy and Cycle Counts
text:
### roles.ch03.s1 3.1 Stock Controller - Inventory Accuracy and Cycle Counts

1. The Stock Controller owns inventory accuracy day to day for Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow. The role is accountable for the integrity of stock in the system matching stock on the rack across the 6,000 m2 hall and all six zones A-F, working Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and any authorised Saturday morning peak overtime under direction of the Shift Supervisor on duty and overall accountability of the Warehouse Manager. Two Stock Controllers cover the operation.

2. The Stock Controller plans and executes cycle counts every working day on a rotating zone schedule under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. This includes Zone A receiving, Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 pallet positions, Zone C picking, Zone D dispatch, Zone E cold zone and Zone F services including the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage. No working day passes without cycle counts, and coverage ensures every location is counted on rotation.

3. All counts are performed strictly via the handheld WMS scanners against system-directed tasks. The Stock Controller uses the 20 shared scanners, ensures scan verification for every location, product, batch and quantity, and logs count results, variances and recounts. No manual adjustment or bypass of scanner control is permitted.

4. The Stock Controller enforces the second-count rule without exception: no inventory adjustment is ever posted without a second count. Any variance found on first count is recounted by a second person, normally the second Stock Controller or the Shift Supervisor, before any adjustment is proposed. The Stock Controller does not post adjustments unilaterally; adjustments are proposed with evidence and approved through the control hierarchy.

5. The Stock Controller investigates all variances. This includes recounting, checking adjacent locations, reviewing recent inbound receipts in Zone A, put-away to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F under PR-02, replenishment of Zone C under PR-03, picks under PR-04 and dispatch staging in Zone D, and checking quarantine in Zone F. Damaged goods found are moved to quarantine the same day under PR-09 and logged for disposition; the Stock Controller does not approve write-offs.

6. The Stock Controller supports the annual wall-to-wall stocktake. Once a year the site shuts down for a full stocktake that is personally signed off by the Warehouse Manager only. The Stock Controller prepares locations, ensures Zone C faces are clear, Zone B bays are accessible, Zone E and the hazmat cage are counted within limits, and all pre-count movements are frozen. The role leads counting teams, controls second counts, reconciles variances and compiles the results pack for Manager sign-off.

7. The Stock Controller maintains count discipline around physical and operational limits. This includes the maximum pallet weight of 900 kg, maximum of 2,700 kg per rack bay, block-stacking limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m, and a maximum of 4,000 kg (4 full-weight pallets) in the hazmat cage in Zone F at any time. Hazmat is counted only in the cage and only within authorised quantities.

8. The Stock Controller ensures compliance with site procedures and safety controls relevant to counting. This includes PR-08, PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, PR-11 Pedestrian safety, PR-12 Cold-chain handling for Zone E held at +2 °C to +6 °C, and PR-15 End-of-shift handover. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory on the warehouse floor at all times; speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones are observed. The role does not authorise forklift operators, approve overtime or sign off stocktake results; those authorities rest with the Warehouse Manager, and write-offs up to and including 750 EUR rest with the Shift Supervisor.

9. The Stock Controller hands over under PR-15, reporting daily count completion by zone, open variances requiring second counts, proposed adjustments pending approval, quarantine quantities and readiness for the next rotating count. Where a procedure conflicts with the owner brief, the brief prevails.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Specialist Functions and Site-Wide Standards
title: 3.2 Returns and Packing Staff - Returns Inspection and Packing
text:
### roles.ch03.s2 3.2 Returns and Packing Staff - Returns Inspection and Packing

1. The Returns and Packing Staff are responsible for returns inspection, quarantine control and value-added packing in Zone F (600 m2) at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow. Four staff cover this function across both shifts Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and any authorised Saturday morning peak overtime, under direction of the Shift Supervisor on duty and overall accountability of the Warehouse Manager.

2. The role operates exclusively in Zone F services and control, which contains returns inspection, quarantine, value-added packing and the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2. No returns activity is performed outside Zone F, and hazmat is stored only in the cage with a maximum of 4,000 kg (4 full-weight pallets) at any time. No returns goods are moved to Zone B, Zone C or Zone E without an approved disposition.

3. All returns are handled under PR-07 Returns handling. Returns are accepted only within 14 days of delivery through Zone F. The Returns and Packing Staff receive, identify and log every return against the original delivery, customer and reason code via the handheld WMS scanner. No return is accepted without documentation and Shift Supervisor notification.

4. Every unit returned is inspected. Inspection in Zone F covers quantity, product identity, batch and expiry where applicable, packaging integrity, labelling, seal condition and evidence of damage, contamination, temperature abuse or tampering. For goods destined for Zone E, cold-chain history is checked under PR-12. No unit bypasses inspection and no disposition is made before inspection is complete.

5. Following inspection, the Returns and Packing Staff propose a single disposition for each unit: restock to stock, rework (relabel, repack or clean) or scrap. The proposal is recorded in the system with inspection evidence and reason. The role does not authorise the final decision; final disposition of inspected returns is approved only by the Shift Supervisor. Approved restock is authorised only for saleable, in-date, undamaged product in original condition.

6. Non-conforming, damaged or suspect goods are controlled under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Such goods are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, clearly identified, segregated and logged, and never co-mingled with saleable stock. Write-offs up to and including 750 EUR are approved by the Shift Supervisor; any write-off above 750 EUR requires approval by the Warehouse Manager. No goods leave quarantine without documented approval.

7. The Returns and Packing Staff perform all value-added packing and rework under PR-05 Packing and labelling. This includes repacking, relabelling, kitting and palletisation as instructed by the system and customer instruction, operation of the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers and use of the cardboard baler for waste. Every packed carton and pallet is scan-verified and labelled with correct product, batch, quantity and destination data. A pallet including load may weigh at most 900 kg, and free block-stacking where used is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m.

8. The role observes all site safety and operating limits. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory on the warehouse floor at all times without exception. Speed limits of 8 km/h inside the building, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are observed, and the 1.2 m physically separated pedestrian walkways with yellow barriers are never blocked. MHE is operated only where the individual holds personal authorisation from the Warehouse Manager under PR-10, with a documented pre-use check before first use each day; otherwise movements are by hand pallet jack or electric pallet jack as authorised.

9. Work is performed in accordance with PR-05, PR-07, PR-09, PR-11 Pedestrian safety, PR-13 Hazmat handling where applicable and PR-15 End-of-shift handover. The role logs all inspections, dispositions, quarantine movements and packing completed, and hands over open returns, quarantine status, packing priorities and equipment readiness. Where a procedure conflicts with the owner brief, the brief prevails.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Specialist Functions and Site-Wide Standards
title: 3.3 Maintenance Technician - Equipment, Racking and Dock Maintenance
text:
### roles.ch03.s3 3.3 Maintenance Technician - Equipment, Racking and Dock Maintenance

1. The Maintenance Technician is the sole specialist responsible for the maintenance, safety and availability of all materials handling equipment, racking and dock equipment at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow. The role covers the 6,000 m2 hall, the 3,500 m2 fenced yard and all six zones A-F, working Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and any authorised Saturday morning peak overtime under direction of the Shift Supervisor on duty and overall accountability of the Warehouse Manager.

2. The Technician maintains the complete site asset base. This includes 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t for the high bays in Zone B, 11 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks, 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, 1 cardboard baler, 8 dock levellers at 1.2 m height serving doors 1-8, and racking providing 2,400 pallet positions in Zone B. The Technician does not maintain the 20 handheld WMS scanners beyond physical care and battery replacement reporting.

3. The Technician executes planned preventive maintenance to manufacturer schedules for all MHE, levellers, stretch wrappers, baler and racking. Every truck receives a documented check before its first use each day by its operator under PR-10; the Technician verifies that checks are logged, rectifies defects, and immobilises and tags any truck with a safety-critical defect. No defective truck is returned to service until cleared and logged by the Technician.

4. The Technician maintains storage and dock infrastructure within site limits. This includes high-bay racking in Zone B limited to 2,700 kg per rack bay, free block-stacking limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m, the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F limited to 4,000 kg (4 full-weight pallets) at any time, and pallet weight limited to 1,000 kg inclusive. Damaged racking, barriers, levellers or barriers are quarantined, repaired or replaced the same day where possible and always logged.

5. All reactive repairs are logged without exception. The Technician records every repair with date, time, asset identity, fault found, parts used, action taken and return-to-service sign-off, and reports recurring faults and downtime to the Shift Supervisor and Warehouse Manager. Spare parts, batteries and consumables are controlled and accounted for, and no makeshift repair that compromises capacity or safety is permitted.

6. The Technician conducts the documented monthly racking safety inspection under PR-10 and reports results to the Warehouse Manager. The inspection covers uprights, beams, locking pins, bracing, floor fixings, bay load notices and barrier integrity, with defects categorised, quarantined and tracked to close-out. Cold-zone equipment in Zone E (+2 °C to +6 °C) and ventilation in the hazmat cage are checked for correct operation and alarms.

7. The Technician supports the site safety regime. This includes maintaining fire, alarm and emergency systems in serviceable condition, assisting the Shift Supervisor in the quarterly evacuation drill under PR-14 with roll call at the assembly point by the north fence before re-entry, and ensuring transport aisles of 4.0 m and rack aisles of 3.0 m and the 1.2 m yellow-barrier pedestrian walkways are kept clear of maintenance activity.

8. The Technician complies with all site safety and procedural controls. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory on the warehouse floor at all times; seat belts are worn whenever operating a truck. Speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are observed. Work is performed under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, PR-11 Pedestrian safety, PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response and PR-14 as applicable.

9. The Technician does not hold authorities reserved to others: only the Warehouse Manager authorises new forklift operators, approves overtime and signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake, and only the Shift Supervisor approves write-offs up to and including 750 EUR. The Technician hands over under PR-15 End-of-shift handover, reporting equipment availability, open defects, racking actions and next-shift priorities. Where a procedure conflicts with the owner brief, the brief prevails.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Specialist Functions and Site-Wide Standards
title: 3.4 All Roles - Hours, PPE, Authorisations and General Compliance
text:
### roles.ch03.s4 3.4 All Roles - Hours, PPE, Authorisations and General Compliance

1. Every employee works within the site shift pattern of Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 across the 6,000 m2 hall and 3,500 m2 fenced yard. One Shift Supervisor is in charge of the floor at all times. Peak-season Saturday morning overtime is worked only when authorised in advance by the Warehouse Manager; no other person may approve overtime.

2. Attendance, punctuality and handover apply to all roles. Each employee starts and ends work at the assigned shift time, completes the documented pre-shift briefing as instructed by the Shift Supervisor on duty, and hands over open tasks, equipment status and safety issues under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. No employee leaves an unsafe condition or open incident unreported at end of shift.

3. Personal protective equipment is mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor without exception. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are worn at all times in the hall, yard dock areas and all six zones A-F. Forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. No person enters the floor without correct PPE, and the Shift Supervisor stops work where PPE is not worn.

4. All personnel observe site movement rules. Speed limits are 8 km/h inside the building, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet, including marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide, physically separated by yellow barriers and are never driven on, blocked or used for storage. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m and rack storage aisles of 3.0 m are kept clear at all times.

5. Dock discipline applies to all. Doors 1-4 are inbound only and doors 5-8 are outbound only at 1.2 m dock height, and only the Dispatcher assigns a carrier a door and time slot. Drivers wait in the marked waiting area and never enter the hall. No employee directs a vehicle to a door or allows unloading or loading outside the assigned slot without Dispatcher and Shift Supervisor agreement.

6. No person operates materials handling equipment without personal authorisation. Only the Warehouse Manager authorises new forklift operators to operate MHE under the principle "no licence, no truck", and every truck receives a documented check before its first use each day under PR-10. The site fleet is 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t, 11 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks. Defective equipment is tagged, immobilised and reported immediately to the Shift Supervisor and Maintenance Technician.

7. All roles respect load and storage limits. A pallet including load may weigh at most 1,000 kg. Each rack bay in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg; free block-stacking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m. The 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F holds at most 4,000 kg (4 full-weight pallets) at any time and hazmat is stored only in the cage. Any overload is stopped, grounded and escalated.

8. Temperature and hazmat awareness are required of every employee. Zone E cold zone is held between +2 °C and +6 °C with alarms and a manual temperature verification each shift under PR-12; any employee observing an alarm, door left open or temperature deviation reports it immediately to the Shift Supervisor. No employee handles, moves or stores hazmat outside PR-13, and any spill, leak or damaged hazmat is isolated, cordoned and reported at once without attempt to clean beyond training. Damaged or suspect goods are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09.

9. Inventory and procedural compliance apply to all. No inventory adjustment is ever posted without a second count, cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule under PR-08, and the annual wall-to-wall stocktake is signed off only by the Warehouse Manager. Racking receives a documented safety inspection every month and an evacuation drill under PR-14 with roll call at the assembly point by the north fence is conducted every quarter before re-entry. Every incident is documented and reviewed by the Shift Supervisor.

10. All employees work in accordance with the fifteen site procedures PR-01 to PR-15 and with instructions from the Warehouse Manager and Shift Supervisor. No employee approves write-offs, final stocktake results or overtime outside the reserved authorisations: write-offs above 750 EUR and overtime and new MHE authorisations rest with the Warehouse Manager only, write-offs up to and including 750 EUR and final disposition of inspected returns rest with the Shift Supervisor, and dock scheduling rests with the Dispatcher. Where a procedure conflicts with the owner brief, the brief prevails.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 — Inbound and Outbound Service Levels
title: 1.1 Receiving Windows and Cut-Offs
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. operates inbound receiving in Zone A (800 m²) through Doors 1-4 only. Doors 1-4 are designated inbound only and Doors 5-8 are outbound only; no inbound activity will be allocated or accepted at an outbound door. All receiving is performed in accordance with PR-01 Inbound Receiving and is supervised by the shift supervisor on duty.

2. Standard receiving hours are Monday to Friday, 06:00-22:00, across two shifts (06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00). Receiving outside these hours, including Saturday morning overtime in peak season, is by prior written agreement only and requires approval for overtime from the Warehouse Manager. The last inbound time slot on each shift is scheduled to allow completion of document checks, unloading, counting and inspection within the shift.

3. All inbound deliveries require a pre-booked time slot and dock door allocation from the Dispatcher. The Dispatcher owns dock scheduling and assigns every carrier a specific door (1-4) and time slot. Carriers must report to the marked waiting area in the yard; drivers are not permitted in the hall or beyond Zone A at any time. Unscheduled arrivals will be accommodated only where a Door 1-4 slot and labour are available and will otherwise be rescheduled to the next available slot.

4. No goods move past Zone A until paperwork is checked. The inbound document-to-booking sequence is mandatory and is applied to every delivery without exception:
a) document verification at the assigned door before unloading;
b) unloading, counting and inspection in Zone A;
c) WMS booking only after inspection;
d) put-away to Zone B, E or F only after booking.
Inspected goods only are booked into the system, and booked goods only are released for put-away. This sequence is executed by Inbound Operators (unload, count and inspect) supported by Forklift Operators for mechanical handling, under the direction of the shift supervisor.

5. For document verification, the driver must present the delivery documentation for the purchase order or inbound reference. Unloading will not commence until quantities, product references and visible condition are checked against the documentation. Any discrepancy, damage in transit or missing paperwork is recorded at the door, notified to the shift supervisor and the client, and the affected quantity is held in Zone A pending instruction. Goods are not booked while under query.

6. Service commitment for booking: where correct documentation is presented at the booked slot and the delivery is within the agreed pallet quantity for that slot, counting, inspection and WMS booking will be completed within the same shift. The client will be notified the same working day of any shortage, overage or damage found during count and inspection, and quarantined quantities under PR-09 will not be shown as available stock. Put-away from Zone A to the allocated storage zone will then follow under PR-02.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 — Inbound and Outbound Service Levels
title: 1.2 Dispatch Times and Load Release
text:
### sla.ch01.s2 1.2 Dispatch Times and Load Release

1. Outbound dispatch operates exclusively in Zone D (900 m²) through Doors 5-8. Doors 5-8 are outbound only and Doors 1-4 are inbound only; no outbound loading will be allocated to an inbound door. Only wrapped, labelled pallets are permitted in Zone D staging. All dispatch activity is performed in accordance with PR-05 Packing and Labelling and PR-06 Outbound Dispatch under the supervision of the shift supervisor on duty.

2. Standard dispatch hours are Monday to Friday, 06:00-22:00 across two shifts (06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00). Dispatch outside these hours, including Saturday morning overtime in peak season, is by prior written agreement only and requires overtime approval from the Warehouse Manager. Outbound time slots are assigned by the Dispatcher, who owns dock scheduling and allocates every carrier a specific door (5-8) and time slot. Drivers report to the marked waiting area in the yard and are not permitted in the hall.

3. Packing verification is mandatory before any pallet enters Zone D. Every item picked in Zone C against a WMS scanner task is scan-verified before packing in accordance with PR-04 Order Picking, then packed and labelled in accordance with PR-05. Labelling, quantities and order reference are checked at the packing station; pallets with missing scans, label errors or quantity discrepancies are not transferred to Zone D and are held in Zone C pending correction by the picking team.

4. Pallets moved to Zone D are wrapped using the two semi-automatic stretch wrappers and staged by outbound door. Staging is by door, load and delivery route, with wrapped status and door allocation visible in the WMS. The shift supervisor ensures Zone D segregation is maintained and that unwrapped or unlabelled pallets are not presented for loading. Handling between Zone C and Zone D is performed by Forklift Operators using electric trucks and pallet jacks.

5. No load is loaded or sealed until formally released by the Dispatcher. Load release confirms: a) all pallets for the consignment are scan-verified, packed, labelled and wrapped; b) pallet count and total weight comply with the pallet limit of 900 kg per pallet (load included) and carrier limits; c) documentation and seals are prepared. Once released, the assigned outbound team loads the trailer at the allocated door, and the Dispatcher records door, carrier, seal number and time of departure.

6. Committed outbound capacity per shift is 4 outbound doors × 4 trailer loads per door = 16 trailer loads, equivalent to 448 pallets at full weight (28 × 900 kg pallets per 26,000 kg / 33-position curtain-side trailer). Orders with complete stock available in Zone C that are released to picking before the agreed shift cut-off will be packed, staged in Zone D and made available for their allocated outbound slot within the same shift. Orders released after the cut-off, or requiring replenishment from bulk storage, cold zone or hazmat cage handling, will be scheduled to the next available outbound slot. The delivery van (1,800 kg / 6 positions) is limited to two full-weight (900 kg) pallets per load; any consignment exceeding 900 kg per pallet or 1,800 kg total is allocated to trailer capacity.

7. Pallets exceeding the 900 kg limit, overweight or incorrectly balanced loads, and hazmat loads exceeding the cage limit of 4,000 kg (4 full-weight pallets at 900 kg) will not be released. Such pallets are held in Zone D quarantine area and notified to the client and shift supervisor for instruction before rescheduling.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 — Inbound and Outbound Service Levels
title: 1.3 Dock Scheduling and Transport Capacity
text:
### sla.ch01.s3 1.3 Dock Scheduling and Transport Capacity

1. All dock activity is scheduled centrally by the Dispatcher. The Dispatcher owns dock scheduling and assigns every carrier a specific door and time slot in advance: Doors 1-4 for inbound only (Zone A) and Doors 5-8 for outbound only (Zone D). No vehicle is accepted without a confirmed slot and door allocation. Carriers must report to the marked waiting area in the fenced yard (3,500 m²) and drivers are not permitted in the hall at any time.

2. Yard and building movements are governed by PR-10 Forklift and MHE Operation and PR-11 Pedestrian Safety in the Warehouse. Speed limits are enforced at all times: 8 km/h inside the building, 12 km/h in the yard, and 5 km/h at all pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Pedestrian walkways are physically separated by yellow barriers and are 1.2 m wide. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and rack storage aisles are 3.0 m; blocking of aisles or dock approaches is not permitted.

3. Standard dock operating hours are Monday to Friday, 06:00-22:00 over two shifts (06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00). Slot times are set to allow full completion of inbound document check, unloading, count and inspection in Zone A, or outbound wrapping, staging and loading in Zone D, within the allocated shift under PR-01 and PR-06. Saturday morning overtime in peak season and any work outside standard hours is by prior written agreement only and requires overtime approval from the Warehouse Manager.

4. Promised transport capacity is calculated on the site pallet limit of 900 kg per pallet, load included. Each contracted curtain-side trailer carries a maximum of 26,000 kg on 33 floor positions, which equates to 28 full-weight (900 kg) pallets per trailer. Trailers are loaded only to this weight limit regardless of available floor positions. The delivery van carries a maximum of 1,800 kg on 6 positions, which equates to two full-weight pallets per van load; any consignment exceeding 900 kg per pallet or 1,800 kg total is allocated to trailer capacity.

5. Committed throughput per shift is determined by outbound dock capacity: 4 outbound doors (5-8) × 4 trailer loads per door per shift = 16 trailer loads per shift, equivalent to 448 full-weight pallets per shift. Inbound capacity through Doors 1-4 is planned on the same 4-loads-per-door-per-shift basis to protect put-away and replenishment flows to Zones B, E and F. Each dock door is equipped with its own dock leveller (1.2 m dock height). Where client volumes exceed committed throughput, additional loads are scheduled to the next available shift slot by the Dispatcher.

6. Slot adherence is mandatory. Late arrivals of more than 30 minutes, no-shows or arrivals with incorrect or incomplete documentation will forfeit the allocated slot and be rescheduled to the next available slot for the correct door type (inbound 1-4 or outbound 5-8). Unscheduled arrivals are accepted only where a suitable door, labour and MHE are available within the current shift without disrupting booked loads, and otherwise are rescheduled. The Dispatcher records all arrivals, door allocations, slot times and departure times in the WMS.

7. The Dispatcher sequences doors to maintain one-way flow: inbound only at Doors 1-4 direct to Zone A (800 m²) and outbound only at Doors 5-8 from Zone D (900 m²). No inbound unloading is permitted at an outbound door and no outbound loading at an inbound door. Forklift Operators and Inbound Operators handle mechanical moves using the electric fleet under shift supervisor control, and drivers must remain in the waiting area during dock operations for safety and security.

title: 2.1 Order Accuracy and Picking Service Level
text:
### sla.ch02.s1 2.1 Order Accuracy and Picking Service Level

1. All order picking is performed exclusively in Zone C (1,200 m²) from ground-level pick faces and flow racks. No picking is performed directly from bulk storage in Zone B, from the cold zone in Zone E or from the hazmat cage in Zone F except as a documented exception authorised by the shift supervisor. All picking tasks are generated and directed by the WMS and executed with the 20 handheld WMS scanners. Paper-based or verbal picks are not permitted.

2. Every unit picked in Zone C is scan-verified in accordance with PR-04 Order Picking before packing. The picker scans the pick-face location and each item barcode against the WMS task; the system validates product reference and quantity in real time. Any scan mismatch, short pick or damaged stock found at the face is not packed. The picker flags the exception in the scanner, the location is blocked in the WMS, and the shift supervisor and Stock Controller are notified for recount and reallocation to the next available stock.

3. Pick faces in Zone C are replenished from bulk storage in Zone B (2,200 m², 2,400 pallet positions) under PR-03 Replenishment of Pick Faces before the start of each picking shift. Replenishment tasks are system-triggered on minimum levels and are completed and confirmed before pickers are released to that aisle. Replenishment is performed by Forklift Operators using electric counterbalance forklifts (3.0 t), reach trucks (2.0 t) and electric pallet jacks, respecting the site pallet limit of 900 kg per pallet and the rack bay limit of 2,700 kg. A pick face showing zero or low-stock in the WMS will not be picked until replenishment is confirmed or an alternative face is assigned.

4. Packing and labelling accuracy is enforced under PR-05 Packing and Labelling. Every picked item is scan-verified before packing, then packed and labelled at the designated packing station in Zone C. Label data, order reference and quantity are verified against the WMS order at the station. Pallets are only transferred to Zone D dispatch staging when fully packed, correctly labelled and wrapped; pallets with missing scans, label errors or quantity discrepancies are held in Zone C pending correction.

5. Picking, replenishment and packing are supervised by the shift supervisor on duty, who controls floor staff and scanner allocation across the two shifts Monday to Friday 06:00-22:00. Pickers execute scanner tasks; Stock Controllers own day-to-day inventory accuracy for Zone C faces and investigate repeated pick exceptions. The Dispatcher releases outbound loads only after scan-verified status is confirmed in the WMS.

6. Harborwick 3PL measures picking service level as correctly picked, scan-verified order lines versus total order lines shipped in the reporting period. Shortages caused by physical stock unavailability after replenishment, client master-data errors, or late client order amendments after picking release are recorded as exceptions and excluded from the picking accuracy calculation. Accuracy results and exception reasons are reported to the client monthly and retained with WMS scan logs for audit.

7. Any mis-pick, mis-label or quantity error identified before dispatch is corrected in Zone C, re-scanned and re-labelled before release to Zone D. Errors identified after dispatch are logged as incidents, reviewed by the shift supervisor under PR-04/PR-05, and notified to the client the same working day with corrective action, including re-pick, replacement or credit as agreed.

title: 2.2 Stock Counts, Reconciliations and Adjustments
text:
### sla.ch02.s2 2.2 Stock Counts, Reconciliations and Adjustments

1. Inventory accuracy is maintained under PR-08 Stocktaking and Cycle Counts. The principle that the stock in the system is the stock on the rack is enforced by continuous counting, a mandatory second count before any adjustment, and formal sign-off. All counts are directed by the WMS and executed with the handheld WMS scanners; Stock Controllers own inventory accuracy day to day including cycle counts, recounts and adjustments, under the supervision of the shift supervisor on duty.

2. Cycle counts run every working day, Monday to Friday, on a rotating zone schedule covering Zones A to F. The schedule is published weekly by the Stock Controllers and approved by the shift supervisor to ensure each zone is counted regularly, with priority given to high-movement pick faces in Zone C, bulk storage in Zone B, the cold zone in Zone E and the hazmat cage in Zone F. Counts are blind counts: the counter scans location and product without seeing system quantity, and the WMS validates after submission. Inbound receiving in Zone A and dispatch staging in Zone D are counted within the same rotation; goods in quarantine or held pending inspection are counted but remain flagged as unavailable.

3. The annual wall-to-wall stocktake is a full physical count of all pallet positions and pick faces across all six zones. The site is shut down for the duration of the count on a date agreed in advance with clients. All 2,400 bulk pallet positions in Zone B, pick faces in Zone C, the 300 m² cold zone, the 60 m² hazmat cage and staging areas in Zones A, D and F are counted by teams of Stock Controllers, Inbound Operators and Pickers assigned by the shift supervisor. Forklift Operators support high-bay access using the electric fleet in accordance with PR-10, respecting the pallet limit of 900 kg and the rack bay limit of 2,700 kg. The result is reconciled by the Stock Controllers and submitted for sign-off.

4. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. Where a first count differs from the WMS, the system blocks the location and generates a recount task assigned to a second person who was not the first counter, wherever staffing allows, or to the Stock Controller. Only when the second count is posted is a variance confirmed. Unconfirmed variances are escalated to the shift supervisor for investigation, including checks of replenishment, put-away and dispatch transactions in the WMS.

5. Reconciliations and adjustments are documented in the WMS with reason code, location, product reference, quantity, counter identities and count times. Small variances are investigated for transaction error, misplacement or damage before any stock correction. Adjustments are posted only after the second count and review: the Stock Controller proposes the adjustment, and the shift supervisor reviews and approves incident reports and inventory adjustments arising from cycle counts. The Warehouse Manager is accountable for the whole site and signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results; any inventory write-off for damaged goods above 750 EUR also requires Warehouse Manager sign-off, while write-offs up to 750 EUR may be approved by the shift supervisor.

6. Clients are notified of confirmed variances affecting available stock on the same working day, and quarantined or damaged quantities are not shown as available stock. Cycle count coverage, hit-rate and adjustment logs, and the annual stocktake reconciliation are retained for audit and summarised in monthly inventory reporting.

title: 2.3 Operating Hours and Inventory Reporting
text:
### sla.ch02.s3 2.3 Operating Hours and Inventory Reporting

1. Standard operating hours are Monday to Friday, 06:00-22:00, across two shifts: mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00. All warehouse operations — inbound receiving in Zone A, put-away and replenishment to Zones B, E and F, picking in Zone C, and dispatch staging in Zone D — are performed only within these hours and in accordance with PR-15 End-of-Shift Handover and the applicable procedure PR-01 to PR-14. The WMS is the system of record and is updated in real time during operating hours.

2. Each shift is led by one shift supervisor who is in charge of the floor, floor staff and incident response for that shift. The Warehouse Manager is accountable for the whole site — operations, safety and final sign-offs — and is not routinely present on both shifts but remains the escalation point for operational decisions.

3. No work is performed outside standard hours. Saturday morning overtime in peak season, extended receiving or dispatch windows, and any ad-hoc work beyond 06:00-22:00 Monday to Friday is by prior written agreement with the client only. Only the Warehouse Manager approves overtime; shift supervisors, dispatchers and stock controllers cannot authorise overtime or commit out-of-hours resources.

4. A documented end-of-shift handover is completed at 14:00 and at 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor records completed receipts, put-aways, replenishments, picks, dispatches and cycle counts, open exceptions, equipment defects and quarantine movements, and hands over to the incoming shift supervisor. Open inbound queries in Zone A, pending put-away to Zone B/E/F, and staged loads in Zone D are carried forward with door allocations and WMS references until closed.

5. Stock availability in the WMS is live during operating hours. Only inspected goods booked after count and inspection in Zone A are shown as available; goods in quarantine, damaged-goods hold, or held pending document query are flagged as unavailable and are not allocated to picking. Any confirmed variance arising from cycle counts that affects available quantity is notified to the affected client the same working day under PR-08.

6. Routine inventory reporting is provided as follows:
a) daily system stock position available on request via WMS extract during operating hours;
b) weekly cycle-count plan and completion summary by zone, issued by the Stock Controllers and supervised by the shift supervisor;
c) monthly inventory report issued within five working days of month-end, summarising opening and closing stock by product reference, receipts, dispatches, confirmed adjustments with reason codes, quarantine balances, write-offs approved by the shift supervisor up to 750 EUR or by the Warehouse Manager above 750 EUR, and cycle-count coverage and hit-rate.
All reports are retained with underlying count and adjustment logs for audit.

7. The annual wall-to-wall stocktake is performed on a date agreed in advance with clients during a scheduled site shutdown. The full count across all zones, including all 2,400 pallet positions in Zone B, pick faces in Zone C, the cold zone in Zone E and the 60 m2 hazmat cage in Zone F, is reconciled by the Stock Controllers and signed off by the Warehouse Manager. The signed reconciliation and variance report is issued to each client within ten working days of the count.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 — Damaged Goods, Returns and Temperature-Controlled Storage
title: 3.1 Damaged Goods and Quarantine Handling
text:
### sla.ch03.s1 3.1 Damaged Goods and Quarantine Handling

1. All damaged goods are handled under PR-09 Damaged-Goods Handling and are quarantined in Zone F (600 m²) the same day they are found. This applies wherever damage is identified — during inbound count and inspection in Zone A, from bulk storage in Zone B, at pick faces in Zone C, in dispatch staging in Zone D, from the cold zone in Zone E, or during returns inspection in Zone F — and on any shift, Monday to Friday 06:00-22:00. No damaged stock is left in its original location overnight and no damaged stock is ever shown as available for allocation or picking.

2. On identification, the finder immediately segregates the affected pallet, carton or unit, applies a quarantine label with product reference, quantity, location found, date, time and finder name, and notifies the shift supervisor. The shift supervisor ensures safe mechanical handling by Forklift Operators using the electric fleet in accordance with PR-10, respecting the pallet limit of 900 kg and the rack bay limit of 2,700 kg where applicable, and the goods are moved to the designated quarantine area within Zone F before end of shift.

3. Quarantine in Zone F is physically segregated from value-added packing, returns inspection and the ventilated hazmat cage. Damaged non-hazmat goods are held in the quarantine area only; damaged hazmat is held only inside the separate 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage within Zone F and counts towards the cage limit of 4,000 kg at any time (maximum 4 full-weight pallets at 900 kg). At no time is damaged hazmat stored in general quarantine or in any other zone.

4. On arrival in quarantine, the Stock Controller blocks the quantity in the WMS as unavailable on the same working day, so quarantined stock cannot be allocated to orders, replenishment or dispatch. The WMS record captures quarantine location in Zone F, original location, reason code, photographs where required, and reference to the incident report. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report for damaged goods under PR-09.

5. Inspection and disposition are completed in Zone F. The Stock Controller and, for returns-related damage, the returns and packing staff inspect the quarantine hold, verify quantity and condition, and propose disposition: restock after rework, hold pending client instruction, or scrap/write-off. Returns staff propose restock, rework or scrap for inspected returns; for general damaged-goods quarantine, the Stock Controller proposes the adjustment. No quarantined goods are released back to available stock without inspection and documented approval.

6. Write-off approval thresholds are fixed. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR per incident and the final disposition of inspected returns held in Zone F. Any damaged-goods write-off above 750 EUR requires sign-off by the Warehouse Manager, who is accountable for the whole site and holds final sign-off authority. No adjustment is posted without a second count in accordance with PR-08, and approved write-offs are recorded in the WMS with value, approver name and date.

7. Clients are notified the same working day of any damage affecting their stock, with quantity, product reference, location found and WMS quarantine reference. Quarantined balances are reported as unavailable in daily stock extracts and in the monthly inventory report. All quarantine movements, inspection records, incident reviews and write-off approvals are retained with WMS logs for audit, and any racking damage associated with the incident is reported to the maintenance technician for inspection and logging.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 — Damaged Goods, Returns and Temperature-Controlled Storage
title: 3.2 Returns Handling and Disposition
text:
### sla.ch03.s2 3.2 Returns Handling and Disposition

1. Returns are accepted only within 14 days of the original delivery date, in accordance with PR-07 Returns Handling. The 14-day window is calculated from the WMS proof-of-dispatch date to the physical receipt of the return at Harborwick 3PL. Goods returned after 14 days, without a prior written client authorisation and a returns reference, will not be accepted and will be held pending client instruction. All returns require advance notification to the Dispatcher with product reference, quantity, reason and original delivery reference to allow door allocation.

2. All returns are processed exclusively in Zone F (600 m²) during standard operating hours Monday to Friday 06:00-22:00, under the supervision of the shift supervisor on duty. Returned goods arriving at an assigned inbound door (Doors 1-4) are checked for documentation at receipt, then moved by Forklift Operators to the designated returns inspection area within Zone F. Drivers wait in the marked yard waiting area and are not permitted in the hall. Returns are not booked as available stock on receipt.

3. Every returned unit is inspected in Zone F before any disposition decision. Returns and packing staff inspect quantity, condition, packaging integrity, labelling and, where applicable, sell-by date and temperature indicator for cold-chain goods, in accordance with PR-07 and PR-12. Inspection is recorded in the WMS with photographs where required. Damaged units found during inspection are segregated immediately, labelled, and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09; damaged hazmat is held only inside the separate 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage within Zone F and counts toward the cage limit of 4,000 kg (4 full-weight pallets at 900 kg per pallet).

4. On receipt, the Stock Controller blocks the full returned quantity in the WMS as unavailable, so it cannot be allocated to picking in Zone C, replenishment or dispatch. WMS status remains unavailable throughout inspection and quarantine and is visible in daily stock extracts and monthly inventory reporting. No adjustment is posted without a second count where a quantity variance is identified, in accordance with PR-08.

5. Disposition is proposed only after inspection is complete.
