Returns and packing staff propose one of three dispositions for each inspected unit: restock to available stock, rework/repack in Zone F value-added packing, or scrap/write-off. The proposal is recorded in the WMS with reason code, condition grade and, for rework, required action. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns; this approval authority is fixed and includes release for rework or scrap up to operational value.

6. Restock is executed only after documented approval. Approved units are re-labelled where required, scan-verified, and booked by the Stock Controller as available stock for put-away to Zone B (2,200 m² bulk storage), Zone E (300 m² cold zone, +2 °C to +6 °C) or replenishment to Zone C pick faces under PR-02/PR-03. Units approved for rework are handled in Zone F and re-inspected before booking; units approved for scrap/write-off are held in quarantine until write-off is authorised — up to 750 EUR per incident by the shift supervisor and above 750 EUR by the Warehouse Manager — and then disposed of with a WMS adjustment and audit record.

7. Clients are notified the same working day of receipt, inspection result and approved disposition for their returns, with WMS quarantine and inspection references. All returns movements, inspection records, disposition approvals and any resulting adjustments or write-offs are retained with WMS logs for audit and summarised in the monthly inventory report as quarantine balances and approved write-offs.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 — Damaged Goods, Returns and Temperature-Controlled Storage
title: 3.3 Temperature-Controlled Storage SLA
text:
### sla.ch03.s3 3.3 Temperature-Controlled Storage SLA

1. Temperature-controlled storage is provided exclusively in Zone E (300 m²) and is operated under PR-12 Cold-Chain Handling under the supervision of the shift supervisor on duty. Zone E is physically segregated from Zones A-D and F and is held continuously between +2 °C and +6 °C. No ambient, hazmat or general bulk stock is stored in Zone E, and no cold-chain stock is stored outside Zone E except when in transit between zones under PR-12. All handling in Zone E is performed by trained Forklift Operators and Inbound Operators using electric MHE in accordance with PR-10.

2. Harborwick 3PL commits to maintain the air temperature in Zone E within +2 °C to +6 °C at all times while client product is present, including outside standard operating hours. The chamber is fitted with continuous electronic monitoring and audible/visual alarms that trigger immediately on deviation below +2 °C or above +6 °C. Alarms are monitored by the shift supervisor during operating hours Monday to Friday 06:00-22:00 and, out of hours, alert the Warehouse Manager and maintenance technician on call. Any alarm activation is logged with time, duration, temperature reading and response action.

3. In addition to automated alarms, a manual temperature verification is performed in Zone E on every shift, in accordance with the site practice stated in the warehouse brief. The check is carried out at a defined point in each shift (morning 06:00-14:00 and afternoon 14:00-22:00), recorded on the shift log with thermometer reading, time and operator name, and countersigned by the shift supervisor at handover under PR-15. Electronic logger data and manual verification records are retained for audit and made available to the client on request.

4. Put-away to and from Zone E follows the mandatory goods-flow sequence: document check and inspection in Zone A, WMS booking only after inspection under PR-01, then put-away to Zone E under PR-02. Only inspected and booked goods are placed in Zone E and only booked goods are replenished from Zone E to pick faces in Zone C. The site pallet limit of 900 kg per pallet (load included) and rack bay limit of 2,700 kg apply in Zone E, and pallets are not block-stacked above cold-zone racking specifications.

5. Exposure time outside the +2 °C to +6 °C range is minimised. Door openings, transfer between Zone E and Zone A/C/D/F, and any inspection or picking activity are planned to limit ambient dwell to the minimum required for the task. Picked cold-chain units are scan-verified in Zone C or at the designated cold-chain pack station and returned to Zone E or moved to wrapped Zone D staging without delay. Cold-chain returns are inspected in Zone F under PR-07 with temperature indicator check, and are not returned to Zone E stock without approval.

6. Any temperature excursion, equipment failure or product found outside +2 °C to +6 °C is treated as an incident under PR-12 and PR-09. The shift supervisor is notified immediately, affected pallets are segregated, labelled and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, the quantity is blocked in the WMS as unavailable, and the maintenance technician is called to inspect and log the repair. No affected stock is released as available without inspection and documented approval, and write-off approval follows the fixed thresholds: shift supervisor up to 750 EUR per incident, Warehouse Manager above 750 EUR.

7. Clients are notified the same working day of any excursion or alarm affecting their stock, with product reference, quantity, time, recorded temperatures and WMS quarantine reference. Daily stock extracts show Zone E balances and quarantined cold-chain holds as unavailable, and the monthly inventory report summarises Zone E receipts, dispatches, quarantines, adjustments and logger compliance. Logger data, manual verification logs, alarm records and quarantine dispositions are retained with WMS logs for audit.
